### How a quote is priced

- **Price list** — every quote is priced from one price list *revision*, shown as *List name (Rev. N)*. The quote keeps the prices it was made with, even when an admin later changes the list (see **When prices change** below).
- **Areas** — rooms or parts of the job (a new quote starts with **Area #1**). Each area has a **Quantity**; an area with quantity 2 counts twice (shown as *× 2*).
- **Color options** — the choices you offer the customer (Option 1, Option 2…). Each option sets a material, color and edges for each area, and gets its own total. Areas and options are added in the drawing tool's **5 Color & Edge** step (**Add color option**, **Add area**, **Re-order options**, **Re-order areas**).
- **Lines** — the drawing produces the stone, edge, splash, cutout and other lines from the price list. Extra items (delivery, removal, misc charges…) are added as items on an area or under **Other Items**.
- **Totals per option** = all lines (× area quantity) − **Discount** + **Tax**.
  - **Discount** = *Discount (%)* of the lines that allow a discount, plus *Discount ($)*. It is never more than those lines add up to.
  - **Tax** = *Tax Rate (%)* of the taxable lines only.

---

### Quote Summary (quote page)

The **Quote Summary** card shows:

- **Price List** (with revision) and **Area** (total sq ft).
- One row per color option: number (or **Total** when there is only one option), stone photo, color name(s), material (*No material picked* if none), the option total, and under it each deposit from the payment terms (for example *50% Deposit: $4,200.00*).
- Badges: **Sold out** (a color on the option is sold out; hover for the message), **Low stock** (*Only N slabs in stock; this option needs about M. There might not be enough material.*), **N missing** (lines with no price; hover to see which).
- *Some prices are missing, so these totals are not final. Open an option to see which lines.*

Click an option row (*Show the price breakdown*) to open its breakdown (it also paints the drawing with that stone; click again to clear). **Details** opens or closes the breakdown; the arrows (**Previous color** / **Next color**) step through options. The breakdown lists each area's lines with unit prices, then discount, tax and total. Under **Total** come the deposits from the payment terms (each as dollars) and **Balance Due** (the total minus the deposits; the payment terms' **Remaining** name replaces "Balance Due" when set).

---

### Price Details step (in the drawing tool)

Open the quote → **Edit drawing** → **6 Price Details**.

#### Price Settings

A box at the top shows **Price List** (name and Rev.), **Tax**, **Discount** and **Expires**. Click the pencil (**Edit price settings**) to open **Pricing Settings**:

| Field | What it does |
|-------|--------------|
| **Tax** | Shown when the company has tax rates (Admin > Quotes > Tax Rates). Pick a rate, or **Custom**. |
| **Tax Rate (%)** | The percent, when **Custom** is picked or the company has no tax rates. |
| **Discount (%)** | Percent off the lines that allow a discount. |
| **Discount ($)** | Fixed dollars off, on top of the percent (not negative). |
| **Expiration Date (YYYY-MM-DD)** | Last day the customer can accept online. |
| **Change Price List** (button) | Opens **Select Price List**: pick a list (shown with revision and date) → **Save**. *The quote is re-priced with the latest revision of the selected list.* Extras the new list doesn't offer are removed; its "add to every new quote" extras are added. |

Click **Save**. Pricing settings are stored on the quote right away (they do not need the drawing's **Save**).

New quotes start with the price list's default tax rate and expiration days (30 days if none). If the quote has no price list you see *This quote has no price list…* with a **Choose price list** button.

#### Area tables

Each area (and **Other Items**) has a table with a column per color option: **Product**, **Color** and **Edge #** at the top, then one row per line with its unit price (*@ $59.00/sq ft*) and line total, and a **Subtotal**.

- Pencil (**Edit area**) → **Edit Area**: change the area's name and **Quantity**.
- **+** (**Add item**) → add an extra item to that area (or to Other Items).
- At the bottom, **Total** shows **Discount (…)**, **Tax (…%)** and **Total** for each option. Missing prices show the total in red with *\* Some prices are missing*.

#### Overriding a price

1. Click an underlined unit price (*@ $…*).
2. **Override Price List** shows **Product**, **Price List Price**, and **Override Price List** (type the new price per unit).
3. **Save**. Overridden prices show in blue with ▲ (higher than the list) or ▼ (lower). Clear the field and save to go back to the list price.

Overrides apply to that color option only. Grey, non-underlined prices cannot be overridden, and the informational *… sq ft Countertop - Priced by the slab* line has no price of its own (the slab material line itself can still be overridden).

#### Adding extra items

1. Click **+** on an area or on **Other Items**. **Add Other Item** opens.
2. **Item** — type to search (e.g. *Delivery*); the list comes from the price list's items, grouped by category, plus **<Add Miscellaneous Item>** and **<Add Text Item>** (*No matching item* when nothing fits the search).
3. Depending on the item:
   - **Option** — when the item has options.
   - **Amount (unit)** — for items priced in ranges (e.g. by sq ft). When the item is set to fill from the area, it is filled with the area's sq ft (*Filled from the area. Updates again when the drawing changes.*).
   - **Quantity** — for other items.
   - Miscellaneous items: **Description**, **Price ($)** and checkboxes **Hide On Quote** (the customer doesn't see this line's price, but it still counts in the total), **Allow Discount**, **Taxable**.
   - Text items: just a **Description** (a note line with no price).
4. **Area** — which area the item belongs to, or **Other Items**.
5. **Save**. Click an item's name in the table to change it (**Edit Other Item**) or **Delete** it.

Overrides, items and area changes are part of the drawing: click **Save** in the drawing tool to keep them (this creates a new revision).

---

### Payment terms and deposits

Shown in **Quote Info → Payment Terms** on the quote page, e.g. *50% Deposit · Net 10* (or *(No Deposit)*). Click the text (or the **Terms** pencil inside **Edit Quote Info**) to open **Edit Payment Terms**:

- **Default** (**Default terms**, shown when the company has payment terms in Admin > Quotes > Payment Terms) — pick one to fill the terms text, or **Custom**.
- **Terms** — free text (*Net 10, Due on Receipt, etc.*).
- **Deposits** — choose **Percentage (%)** or **Amount ($)**. **Add** adds a deposit row (starts at 50 / *Deposit*); each row has the amount (**Deposit amount**, empty until you type one), a **Description** (**Deposit description**), and a trash icon (**Remove deposit**).
- **Remaining** — the name of the final payment (printed as *Balance Due* when left empty).
- **Save**.

Where deposits show: under each option total in the Quote Summary, under **Total** in an option's breakdown (with **Balance Due**), and in the **Payment Terms** part of printed quotes and contracts (a percentage deposit also shows its dollar amount when the quote has one option), followed by *Balance Due: remaining balance*. New quotes start with the price list's default payment terms, else the company's first payment terms.

The customer quote page does not take payments; deposits are information on the quote.

---

### When prices change

If the price list, inventory prices or catalog extras changed after the quote was priced, a yellow banner appears on the quote page and in the drawing tool:

*Prices changed since this quote was priced: N lines would change. The quote keeps its prices until you update them.*

- **Show changes** / **Hide changes** — lists each line *old → new*, *new: $…*, or *→ no longer priced*. *(replaces the price typed on the quote)* marks a line whose overridden price would give way to today's price.
- **Update prices** — moves the quote to the list's newest revision and today's prices.

The banner does not appear while viewing an old revision.

---

### Sold out, low stock and missing prices

- **Sold out** — a color marked sold out cannot be on a quote. You can still save the drawing (*… is sold out. You can still save, but pick another color before sending the quote.*), but the customer cannot accept that option until it is changed. Signed quotes keep their colors.
- **Low stock** — fewer slabs in stock than the option needs; only a warning.
- **Missing** — a line has no price (for example *No Product selected.* or *No price available.*). Totals with missing lines are not final.

---

### Common questions / troubleshooting

- **A line shows no price (red). What do I do?** Read the reason under it in **6 Price Details** and fix that: *No Product selected.* or *No Color selected.* → pick them on step **5 Color & Edge**; *Special order: enter a price per sq ft.* → type it in the **Special order** box under **Color**; *Add slabs in the slab layout.* → **Slabs & Layout**; *No fabrication price for …* → an admin sets it in the price list (**Fabrication & install**). Save the drawing.
- **How do I add a discount?** Edit drawing → **6 Price Details** → pencil next to **Price Settings** → **Discount (%)** and/or **Discount ($)** → **Save**.
- **The discount doesn't change the total.** The lines on the quote don't allow discounts (price list setting, or **Allow Discount** unticked on a misc item).
- **How do I change or remove tax?** Same dialog: pick another **Tax** rate, or **Custom** with **Tax Rate (%)** (0 or blank for none). Quote tax is set per quote; the presets come from Admin > Quotes > Tax Rates.
- **How do I extend the expiration date?** **Pricing Settings** → **Expiration Date (YYYY-MM-DD)** → **Save**.
- **How do I switch the price list?** **Pricing Settings** → **Change Price List**, or duplicate the quote onto another list.
- **How do I add delivery, removal or a custom charge?** **+** on an area or **Other Items** → pick the item, or **<Add Miscellaneous Item>** for a custom price.
- **Why does the quote show old prices?** Quotes keep their prices; use **Update prices** on the banner.
- **Can the customer pay the deposit online?** No; deposits are shown on the quote and printouts only.

## Sending, Printing and Selling Quotes

How to get a quote to the customer (email with a link, printed PDF, contract for e-signature), how to see whether they opened it, and how to mark it sold.

**Where to find it:** Employee view → sidebar **Quotes** → open a quote. At the top of the quote page: **Mark as Sold**, and the **Actions** menu with **Print**, **Email**, **Contract** and **Create invoice**. In this section "click **Print**" (or **Email**, **Contract**) means **Actions** → that item. Any user with Employee or Admin access can use them; **Contract** also needs signature access on your user account.

**Related sections:** Employee Quotes (list, quote page, revisions) · Quote Pricing, Tax, Discounts & Payment Terms · Customer Quote Page (what the customer sees).

---

### Emailing a quote

The email does not attach a PDF: it sends a **link** to the quote's customer page, where the customer can view it and preview stones. The page has no signing: to get a signature, send a **Contract**.

1. Open the quote and click **Email**. The **Email Latest Quote Revision** dialog opens.
2. **Template** — starts on the template you send with most (else the company's most used). Click it to open the template list:
   - **Search...** box; **Company** marks company templates (set up by an admin in Admin > Quotes > Email Templates).
   - Your own templates have a pencil (edit) and trash (delete, asks *Are you sure you want to delete "…"?*).
   - Drag the handle to reorder (saved for you); **Reset to Automatic Order** puts it back to most-used first.
   - **Add a Template** creates your own template (only you see it).
   - With no templates at all, the email starts with the subject *Your countertop quote* and *Here is a quote for your counters:* plus the link. If you delete the selected template, the picker shows **No template** and the email is blank.
3. **Form** (only when the company has quote forms) — which company form the customer sees the quote in. The eye icon (**Preview**, *Preview form*) opens that form in a new tab.
4. **To** — prefilled with the quote's email; type more addresses (suggestions come from your customers). **Cc** and **Bcc** buttons add those rows (*Bcc: Hidden from everyone else on this email.*); the **X** (**Remove Cc field** / **Remove Bcc field**) removes them.
5. **Subject** and message. `[QuoteName]` is replaced with the quote name. `[QuoteLink]` or `[PDFLink]` becomes a tracked **View your quote** link; if the message has no link, one is added at the end.
6. Click **Send**. It stays disabled with *Add a recipient in To to send.* or *Add a subject to send.* until both are filled.

**What happens when you send:**

- The email goes from your email address when it is on the company's email domain (otherwise from the system address); replies come to **you**.
- The email is listed in the **Email** table on the quote with the revision sent and the quote's expiration date.
- If the customer's open deal is in a **Not Contacted Yet** or **Contacted** stage, it moves to **Got a Quote** (when that deal group has a Got a Quote stage).
- If the email could not be sent you see *Could not send the email. Try again.* and nothing is recorded.

#### Your own email templates

**Add a Template** (or the pencil on your template) opens **New template** / **Edit template**:

- **Name** (e.g. *Follow up*), **Subject**, **Message** — all required.
- **Insert Variable** adds the customer's name, the quote total, color, link, expiration date and more. In the message they look like `{{customer.first_name}}`.
- `[QuoteName]`, `[QuoteLink]`, `[PDFLink]` work as above; a template saved without a link gets `[PDFLink]` added at the end.
- **Create** / **Save**. The new template is selected in the email.

Quote variables: **Quote name**, **Quote total** and **Quote material and color** (the option the customer accepted, else the first option), **Quote link**, **Quote expiration date**. If a quote or deal variable has nothing to fill it with yet (for example no price or no deal amount), the email is refused with a message naming the variable; fill it in or remove it and send again.

---

### Seeing what happened to sent emails

Once a quote is emailed, an **Email** table appears at the bottom of the quote page:

| Column | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| **Sent** | Date and time sent. |
| **Recipients** | Who it went to. |
| **Subject** | Click it (*Show the message*) to see the message exactly as sent. **Link off** tag = the link was deactivated. |
| **Revision** | Revision number sent (**Draft** if never saved). |
| **Views** | How many times the customer opened that email's link; click to see each open with its time and device (*Time not recorded* when an open's time wasn't saved). |
| **Sent By** | Who sent it. |
| **Expiration** | The quote's expiration date when sent. |

The quotes list's **Email Viewed** column shows the last time any emailed link was opened.

**Turning a link off:** click the email's **Subject** → **Deactivate link**. That link now shows *This link is no longer active*. **Activate link** turns it back on.

---

### Sending a quote by text message

The quote page has no button to copy the quote's link or to text the quote. To send it by text:

1. Click **Print**, choose the form and save the PDF (see *Printing a quote or saving a PDF*).
2. Open the customer's conversation in **CRM > SMS** (or the deal's SMS), click the paperclip (**Attach files**) → **Upload from computer** and pick the PDF. (The paperclip is there while SMS attachments are on, the default.)
3. Send the text.

Or email the quote (**Email**): only the emailed link's opens are tracked.

---

### Printing a quote or saving a PDF

1. Click **Print**. The **Print Quote** dialog opens.
2. In **Print quote using**, choose the form:
   - The company's own forms (quote forms first, then contract forms), set up in Admin > Quotes > Forms.
   - If the company has no forms yet, the built-in ones: **Quote (line items)**, **Quote (subtotals only)**, **Quote (total only)**, **Contract**, **Drawing & Layout (no prices)**.
3. Click **Print**. A pop-up window opens with the PDF; print it or save/download it from there (it is named after the quote).

If nothing opens you see *Allow pop-up windows for this site to open the preview.* Allow pop-ups for the site and try again.

Printing is recorded (the deal's History shows **Quote printed** when the quote is linked to that deal) and, like emailing, moves the customer's open deal from **Not Contacted Yet** or **Contacted** to **Got a Quote**.

**What the built-in printed quote shows:** company logo/name, address and website; **Created Date**, **Expiration Date**, **Salesperson** (with phone), **Quote Name**; **Project Info** (customer, phones, email); the drawing (each page break on its own page); price lines for the first color option (none on Drawing & Layout); a **Color Options** table (color, edge, total, per sq ft) when there are several options; **Notes**; **Payment Terms** with each deposit and *Balance Due: remaining balance*; and on **Contract**, **Customer Signature** and **Date** lines plus a **Company Representative** line. When the quote has tax, the totals also show *Total (before tax):*.

The form preview page (eye icon in the Email dialog) also has a **Print / Save as PDF** button.

To email a PDF file instead of a link, print/save the PDF and attach it to a normal email.

---

### Sending a contract for e-signature

1. Click **Contract**.
   - With several contract forms, **Send Contract** asks for the **Contract form** → **Continue**.
   - With one contract form (or none, when the company has no forms at all, using the built-in **Contract**), it starts right away.
2. The contract PDF is built and **Send Contract for Signature** opens:
   - **To** = the quote's email; **Subject** = *Contract - <quote name>*; a short message (*Hi <first name>, Please review and sign the attached contract…*).
   - The PDF is attached and already marked for signature, with the signature and date fields on its signature lines. The signer is whoever is first in **To**.
3. Click **Send**. Toast **Sending email…**, then **Email sent**.

After you change anything in the email (recipients, subject, message or attachments), **Cancel**, **X**, **Esc** or a click outside asks **Discard this email?**: **Keep editing** or **Discard**. An unchanged email closes right away.

The **Contracts** table on the quote page lists each contract: **Document Name** (click to open), **Status** (**Draft**, **Sent**, **Viewed**, **Signed**, **Declined**, **Canceled**), **Sent Date**, **Signed Date**, **Sent To**, **Signer**. Each row's **⋮** menu has **View**, **Download** and **Cancel contract**: it opens the same **Cancel this signature request?** confirmation as Resources > eSignatures (with **Notify the customer by email**), and the status becomes **Canceled**. The red count beside **Contracts** leaves canceled ones out. Only the person who sent a contract can cancel it; signed, declined or already canceled ones show **This contract cannot be canceled** with the reason (*Already signed. Send a new contract to change it.* / *Already declined by the customer.* / *Already canceled.*). Contracts also appear in Resources > eSignatures (shown when the company has e-signatures turned on).

**When the customer signs the contract**, the quote is marked **sold** automatically and the customer's deal is marked won. If the quote has several color options and the customer had not picked one, the button shows **Signed: pick option**: click it and choose which option was sold.

**Contract button problems:**

- Disabled with the hint *Add a contract form in Admin › Quotes › Forms*: the company has forms but none is a contract form.
- **Signatures access required** (*Ask your manager for access to signatures…*): your user account cannot send documents for signing yet.

---

### Marking a quote sold

1. Click **Mark as Sold**.
2. The **Mark as Sold** dialog says *The deal is marked won with the option's total as its amount.*
   - When the quote has no deal and the customer has two or more deals: **Which deal is this sale for?** — pick one of the customer's deals (each shows its list, status and amount, or *No stage*).
   - With several options, choose **Which option was sold?** (each shows its total).
3. Click **Mark as Sold**.

**Missing customer details:** before **Mark as Sold**, **Print** or **Contract**, a quote without the customer's address, phone number or email opens **Missing customer details** (*Before marking the quote sold, add the customer's address, phone number and email.*, or *Before printing…* / *Before sending a contract…*). Fill in the missing fields → **Save & continue** (they are saved on the quote and the action goes on), or **Skip for now** to go on without them.

**Address not found:** before **Print** or **Contract**, the quote's address is checked on Google Maps. It must be a house number, street and city, like *123 Main St, Indianapolis, IN 46202*; the state and ZIP may be left out when Google Maps still finds the address. An address Google Maps can't find (for example a ZIP code alone, or a street with no city) opens **Address not found** (*Google Maps can't find the address "46112". Before printing, fix it: …*) with the address filled in to correct. Type the address or pick a suggestion → **Save & continue**: the new address is checked too (**Checking…**), and one Google Maps still can't find shows *Google Maps can't find this address…* under it and is not saved. An address typed in **Missing customer details** before **Print** or **Contract** is checked the same way. **Skip for now** prints or sends the contract with the old address. If Google Maps can't be reached, the address is not blocked.

**What happens:**

- The quote gets a green check in the list and the button changes to **Sold** (hover shows the option and total).
- The quote's deal is marked **Won** with that option's total as the deal **Amount**. With no deal on the quote, the customer's only deal is used, or the deal picked in **Which deal is this sale for?** when there are several; if the customer has no deal, a new won deal is created for the quote's salesperson. A deal that was already won only gets its amount updated.
- Message: *Quote sold: its deal is marked won.* If no deal could be made: *Quote sold. It has no deal to mark won: add a sales rep to the quote.*
- If the company has **Sale on a win** turned on (**Admin > CRM > Automations**), the **Sell Slab** form opens next, filled in from the quote: customer, deal, seller, project address, and one room per area with its square feet and stone. Pick the slabs and click **Submit**. Closing it keeps the quote sold.
- If the company has **Jobs to Unscheduled** turned on (**Admin > CRM > Automations**), a template job and an installation job (status **Not ready**) are added to the schedule's **Unscheduled** list, once per quote.

**Undo:** click **Sold** → **Undo sale**. The dialog says *Sold: …* (or *This quote is sold.*) and *Undo sale makes the quote active again and reopens its deal.* It also clears the customer's online signature and accepted option. Message: *Sale undone: the deal is open again.*

---

### What happens automatically (summary)

| You or the customer… | Result |
|-----------------------|--------|
| Email the quote | Email listed with views; deal in Not Contacted Yet / Contacted moves to Got a Quote. |
| Print the quote | Print recorded; same deal stage move. |
| Customer opens an emailed link | View counted (time and device kept); **Email Viewed** updates. |
| Customer signs a contract sent from the quote | Quote sold; deal won. |
| Mark as Sold | Quote sold; deal won with the option total. |
| Undo sale | Quote active; deal reopened; online signature cleared. |
