The page has seven cards: **Installers**, **Templates**, **Calendars**, **Week starts on**, **Schedule estimate**, **Job time** and **Customer notifications**. **Schedule estimate** and **Customer notifications** are described in *Schedule customer notifications*. **Installers**, **Templates**, **Calendars**, **Job time** and **Customer notifications** start collapsed; click a card's title to open it. It saves immediately. Every event assigned to that person on the Installations or Templates calendar, past and future, now shows in that color, and so does their dot in the schedule's installer and templater filters. Until a color is chosen, each person gets one automatically.

Empty cards read *No installers yet. Add an installer from Users.* / *No templates yet. ### Calendars

The **Calendars** card lists every calendar of the company, built-in ones first. *Turn a calendar off to hide it from the schedule.*

#### Add a calendar

1. Click **Add calendar** at the bottom of the card.
2. Type the name (**New calendar name**, placeholder *Calendar name, e.g. Service calls*, up to 100 characters).
3. Click **Add** (or **Cancel**).

Names must be unique (*A calendar with that name already exists.*), and *Templates*, *Installations* and *Estimates* are reserved. A new calendar is visible to everyone.

#### Rename a calendar

1. Hover the row and click the pencil (**Rename**).
2. Type the new name and press Enter (or click elsewhere). Escape cancels.

Use the switch at the left of the row. A calendar that is off is greyed out here and disappears from everyone's **Calendars** filter and from the event form's **Calendar** picker. Turn it back on at any time; its events are kept.

#### Hide a calendar from specific people

2. Confirm **Delete "*name*"?** — *The calendar is removed from the schedule for everyone, and its events stop showing. To keep the events, hide the calendar instead.* — with **Delete**.

### Week starts on

*The first day of each week in the week and month views.* Click **Sunday** (the default) or **Monday**. It saves at once and applies to everyone in the company who has not picked their own day with the schedule's gear button (see *Your schedule settings*): the schedule's month and week views, the date pickers of the event form and the month calendar of installers' and template technicians' own schedules.

---

### Job time

*How long a job takes, from its sale.* The schedule uses it in two places: a new event on the Installations or Templates calendar gets its length from the customer's sale (see *Events*), and **Auto-plan** fills an installer's or templater's work days with the waiting jobs (see *Schedule → Auto-plan*).

1. Pick **Installations** or **Templates** at the top of the card. Each has its own rules.
2. Fill in the minutes (empty means 0):
   - **Setup, every job**: fixed minutes added to every job whatever its size (unloading, setting up tools, protecting the floor, cleaning up)
   - **Per sq ft** (the sale's square feet; halves allowed, e.g. 2.5)
   - **Per waterfall**
   - **Per sink**
   - **Per cooktop cutout** (a room with a cooktop, "c/t")
   - **Per room with 4" backsplash**
   - **Per room with full-height backsplash**
   - **Per room with tear-out**
   - **Drive time without an address**: used for a drive when a job has no address, the company address is missing or Google Maps can't measure it.
3. Set the work day (**Work day from** … **to**, shop time; the day starts when the person leaves the shop) and the work days (**Sun** to **Sat**; Monday to Friday by default).
4. Click **Save**. **Saved** confirms it.

How a job's length is worked out: **Setup** + square feet × **Per sq ft** + **Per waterfall** × waterfalls + **Per sink** × sinks + **Per cooktop cutout** × rooms with a cooktop + the backsplash minutes for each room with a 4" or full-height backsplash + **Per room with tear-out** × rooms with tear-out. For example, Setup 45, Per sq ft 2 and Per sink 20 make a 50 sq ft kitchen with one sink 45 + 100 + 20 = 165 minutes (2 h 45 min).

A line under the fields shows the result, e.g. *Example: a 50 sq ft kitchen with 1 waterfall and 1 sink takes 3 h 45 min.* With 3 minutes per sq ft, 30 per waterfall and nothing else, 50 sq ft and one waterfall come to 3 h. Lengths are rounded up to 15 minutes. Until at least one length is set, jobs are not sized from their sales (*Set at least one length to size jobs from their sales.*).

What the sale must hold: its square feet, and per room the **Waterfall** (*no*, *yes*, or a number such as *X 2*), **Backsplash** (*4 inch* or *full height*), **Tear out** and **Stove** (*c/t* for a cooktop), plus its sinks. The schedule uses the event's customer's latest sale that isn't installed yet.

### Creating an event

The **Create Event** panel opens on the right (full screen on phones).

1. **Customer** (top box): start typing a customer's name. After two letters, matching customers are listed; pick one to **link** the customer. The box locks and shows the name; the small **×** (**Remove customer**) unlinks it. **Title** (under it) is the event's name: picking a customer fills in their name, and you can change it to anything (for example *Smith – kitchen*). For an event without a customer just type the title (for example *Shop meeting*).
   - **Phone** and **Email** (under the customer) show the customer's phone and email. Change them when this appointment is arranged through someone else — a spouse, or the homeowner when the customer is a contractor. The changed phone and email are saved on **this event only**: confirmations, customer notifications and appointment reminders for this event go to them, and the customer's own phone and email stay as they are. **Customer's number** / **Customer's email** (shown next to a changed one) puts the customer's back.
2. Turn **All-day** on or off, then set **Starts** and **Ends** (date button plus time). On a timed event, changing **Starts** moves **Ends** to one hour later; adjust **Ends** afterwards if needed.
   - **No date yet** (switch above the dates): the event has no day yet and goes in the schedule's **Unscheduled** list instead of the calendar. Pick its status: **Not ready**, **Called** or **Ready** (the dates and the confirmation are hidden). The **+** next to **Unscheduled** (*Add a customer with no date yet*) opens the form with this switch on. Give it a day later by opening it, by dragging it onto a day in the Month view, or with **Auto-plan**.
   On the Installations and Templates calendars, once the event has a customer with a sale, a line under **Ends** shows *Job time from the sale: 3 h 45 min · 50 sq ft · 1 waterfall · 1 sink* (hover it for how it adds up; set the minutes in **Admin → Schedule → Job time**). A new event with no length yet gets that end at once; otherwise click **Set end** to end it that long after **Starts**.
3. **Calendar** — pick the calendar (required).
4. **Label** — the event's color (Blue, Red, Green, Yellow, Purple, Pink, Orange, Teal, Cyan, Indigo, Lime, Slate). On the **Installations** calendar this row is **Installer**, and on **Templates** it is **Template**: pick the person instead (see below).
5. **Repeat** — see *Repeating events*.
6. **Location** — type at least 3 characters and pick the address. The address is used for directions, the day's map and routes.

8. **Note** — opens a text box for details (up to 10,000 characters; on desktop it opens a **Note** dialog, close it with **OK**).
9. Click **Save**. The toast *Event created successfully.* confirms it.

The panel's **×** closes without saving.

**Why link a customer instead of typing the name?** A linked event shows the customer's current name, phone, email and sales rep in **Event details**; the installer's **Checklist** button fills in that customer; and the company's automatic **Customer notifications** (Admin → Schedule) can only reach events with a linked customer. A typed name is plain text.

#### Assigning an installer or template technician

1. Set **Calendar** to **Installations** (or **Templates**).
2. Click **Installer** (or **Template**) and pick the person. Their color is applied to the event. Pick **Unassigned** to take the person off it.
3. **Save**.

The job then appears on that person's own schedule (installer portal, template portal or **My Schedule**). The lists contain users with the **Installer** or **Template Guy** position; with nobody in them the picker reads *No installers for this company yet.* / *No templates for this company yet.* Add the position in **Admin → Company settings → Users**. Changing the calendar to one without people clears the person.

#### QuickBooks invoice (installations)

When the company's QuickBooks is connected and the calendar is **Installations**, an invoice box appears under the customer:

- Without a linked customer it says *Pick a customer from search to add an invoice.*
- With a customer, their **Outstanding invoices** are listed (**Show all invoices (N)** / **Show outstanding only**). If the customer has exactly one invoice it is linked automatically. Click an invoice to link it.
- A linked invoice shows **Invoice #…** (click to preview the PDF) and *Shown to installers*; the × (**Remove invoice**) unlinks it.
- Messages: *This customer is not in QuickBooks yet.*, *No QuickBooks invoices for this customer.*, *QuickBooks is not connected.*

The installer sees the invoice in the job's details (**View PDF**).

---

### Repeating events

Click **Repeat** and choose **Does not repeat**, **Daily**, **Weekly**, **Monthly**, **Yearly** or **Custom**.

- **Custom:** set **Every** *N* and the unit (**day(s)**, **week(s)**, **month(s)**, **year(s)**), for example every 2 weeks.
- By default a repeat never ends (**Ends: Never · Add end date**). Click it to add an end date (it starts 30 days out; change it in **Ends**). **Never ends** removes the end date again.
- A repeating event is one event shown on many dates. **Edit** and **Delete** always apply to the whole series; there is no "this occurrence only" option. To change one date only, end the series earlier or create a separate event.
- Repeating events do not get the company's automatic customer notifications.

---

### Opening and editing an event (including moving it)

**Drag and drop (Month view, on a computer):**

- Drag an event to another day to move it there: it keeps its times and length (a multi-day event moves by the same number of days). Repeating events can't be dragged; change them in their form.
- Drag a job from **Unscheduled** onto a day (*Open to pick a date, or drag onto a day*): it goes on that day as an all-day event with the status **Scheduled**.
- Drag an event from the calendar onto the **Unscheduled** panel to take it off its day: it goes back to the waiting list as **Not ready**.
- Week and Day views and phones have no dragging: move an event by editing its dates.

**Moving or changing an event in its form:**

1. Click the event (in any view, in search results or in a day's list) to open **Event details**. Under the title, tags show its calendar, its installer or template technician, and the crew's status once they tapped **On my way** or **Completed**.
2. Click **⋮ (More options)** → **Edit**. In a day's list you can click the pencil (**Edit event**) directly.
3. Change any field, for example **Starts** / **Ends** to move it to another day or time, or **Installer** to give it to someone else.
4. Click **Save**. The toast reads *Event updated successfully.* The back arrow returns to the details without saving.

Every change is written to the event's **History** with your name (*Date updated*, *Label updated*, *Location updated*, *Title changed to …*, *Customer changed*, *Customer removed*, *Notes updated*, *Calendar changed*, *Repeat updated*). When an event with appointment reminders is moved, its reminders are re-timed to the new start automatically, and company customer notifications follow the new date.

---

### Copying an event

1. Open the event → **⋮** → **Copy**, or click the copy icon (**Copy event**) in a day's list.
2. A new **Create Event** panel opens with the same customer, dates, calendar, person, label, repeat, location, note and attachments.
3. Change what differs (usually **Starts** / **Ends**), remove attachments you don't want, and **Save**.

The copy also brings over the original's comments and comment files. The original event is not changed.

---

### Deleting an event

1. Open the event → **⋮** → **Delete**. Or click **Delete event** (trash) in a day's list, or the red trash icon that appears when you hover an event in Week or Day view.
2. Confirm in **Delete event** (*Are you sure you want to delete "…"? This action cannot be undone.*) with **Delete**.
3. The toast reads *Event deleted successfully.*

Deleting removes the event from everyone's schedule (for a repeating event, the whole series) and cancels its pending appointment reminders. There is no undo; re-create the event if it was deleted by mistake.

---

### What was sold (Project)

When the event's customer has a sale, the layers button on the right of **Event details** opens **Project**: the stone, address, sold date, seller and area, each room with its sinks and options, and the sale notes. Below them is the customer's sold quote drawing (or their newest open quote); tap it to see it full size, and use the magnifier next to the close button to zoom in. The drawing has no edge symbols or key (unfinished edges are drawn red); under it, each area lists what the crew builds — finished edges with their profile, splashes, sink and cooktop cutouts, sinks, faucet holes, outlets, corners and the area's items. Prices and bump-outs/bump-ins are not shown. Installers and template technicians see the same on their own schedule (**My schedule**).

---

### Comments, photos and files on an event

Open the event; at the bottom of **Event details** type in **Comment** and press Enter (or the send button). The paperclip (**Add file to comment**) uploads photos or documents into the conversation. Your own comments can be edited or deleted from their menu. Installers and template technicians can comment and add photos from their own schedules too, so this is the place to leave job notes for the crew.

Files added in the event form (**Attachments**) are separate from comment files; see them with the **Attachments** button on the right of the details panel. To add or remove form attachments, **Edit** the event.

### Common questions

- **The Customer search finds nobody.** Type at least two letters of the customer's name. The customer must exist in **CRM → Customers**; otherwise type the name in **Title**.
- **"Title is required"** — the **Title** box is empty. Type a title, or pick a customer to fill it in.
- **"Calendar is required"** — choose a **Calendar**.
- **"End date must be on or after start date"** — **Ends** is before **Starts**.
- **There is no Installer field.** It only appears when **Calendar** is **Installations** (and **Template** only on **Templates**).
- **I can't pick a color on an installation.** Assigned installations use the installer's color; an admin changes it in **Admin → Schedule**.
- **The installer doesn't see the job.** Check that the event is assigned to that installer (**Installer** row), not just colored.
- **How do I move only one day of a repeating event?** That isn't possible; edits apply to the whole series.

## My Schedule and the template technician portal

Template technicians (people who measure and template kitchens) get a simple, phone-friendly schedule that shows only the appointments assigned to them: one day at a time or a month calendar, with directions to each job.

---

### Who sees what

| User | Where the schedule is |
|------|----------------------|
| User with the **Template Guy** position (and no Installer position) | Signing in opens the **template portal** (`/templates/{companyId}/schedule`). It is the only page they can open: no sidebar, just the company header with **Logout**. |
| **Super Admin** who also has the **Template Guy** position | Keeps the full CRM; the Employee sidebar gets an extra top-level item **My Schedule** (`/employee/my-schedule`) with the same view. |
| Installers | Their own portal with **Schedule**, **Map** and **Checklist** tabs (see *Installer portal & checklists*). |
| Everyone else | The company calendar: Employee sidebar → **Schedule**. |

A user holding several portal positions lands in the first of Installer, Walk-in, Marketing, Shop Worker, Template Guy. Platform superusers can preview this screen by choosing **Template** in the header's position selector.

**Which appointments appear:** every event assigned to that person, on any calendar. An appointment is assigned by choosing the person in the **Template** field of an event on the **Templates** calendar (see *Schedule events*). Unassigned events never show here.

---

### Using the schedule

#### Picking the day

- The heading shows the date (for example *Tue, Oct 20, 2026*). Click it to open the month and year picker; choosing a month there switches to the month calendar.
- **<** and **>** go to the previous or next day (or month in month mode). **Today** jumps back to today.
- On a phone, swipe left or right anywhere on the page to change the day.
- **Day** / **Month** toggle: **Day** shows only the chosen day's jobs; **Month** adds a month calendar above them. Each date shows up to three dots for its jobs; tap a date to see its jobs. Today is underlined and the chosen day is dark.

#### The day's jobs

Each job is a card, in order (all-day jobs first, then by start time), with:

- its stop number and time (**All day** or *9:00 AM – 10:00 AM*),
- the event title,
- the address,
- the event's description and note,
- **Directions** — opens Google Maps driving directions from where the phone is to that address (shown when the job has an address),
- on your own schedule, **On my way** (today's jobs) and **Completed**. **On my way** marks the job and sends the customer the company's On my way message (a text, or an email when the company has no texting; set up in **Admin → Schedule → Customer notifications → On my way**), once; a toast says whether it went (*The customer got a text.* / *The customer got an email.*) or why not. **Completed** marks the job done. The card then shows the status and its time, e.g. *On my way · 9:42 AM*. Admins looking at someone else's schedule don't get these buttons. In the Granite Phone app, with location allowed (*all the time*), the phone also sets **Arrived** when you reach a job's address and **On my way** for your next job when you drive about half a mile away from the shop or the last job (this automatic On my way sends the customer nothing). Only **Completed** completes a job.

*Nothing scheduled for this day.* means no jobs are assigned to the person that day. If loading fails, *The schedule could not be loaded.* appears with **Try again**.

#### Job details, comments and photos

Tap a card (or its arrow, *Comments, photos, files and invoice*) to open **Event details**, a big window with everything on one page: details, the project, the customer's quote drawings (sold quotes, else the newest quote that isn't lost), attachments, and the comments and history beside them. It shows times, customer phone, email and sales rep (when the event is linked to a customer), description and note, address, attachments and the activity feed. Technicians can type a **Comment** and use the paperclip to add photos or files (for example measurement photos) for the office. There is no Edit, Copy or Delete here; the office changes the appointment on the company **Schedule**.

#### Admins: looking at someone else's schedule

Admins and superusers see a **Whose schedule** list at the top of **My Schedule** or the template portal. Pick a template technician to see their jobs (it starts on yourself if you are on the list). It reads *No template makers* when nobody has the Template Guy position.

---

### Common questions

- **How do I see another person's schedule?** Admins and superusers: **Whose schedule** at the top of **My Schedule** (or the template portal) → pick the template technician. For installers' jobs, filter **Schedule** by installer.
- **The technician can't see an appointment.** Open it on the company **Schedule** and check that **Template** is set to that person (a matching color alone is not enough), and that the date is right.
- **Why don't I have My Schedule in my sidebar?** It only appears for Super Admins who also hold the **Template Guy** position. Other template technicians use the template portal they land on after signing in.
- **Can the technician move or cancel an appointment?** No. They can comment on it; office staff edit it on the **Schedule**.
- **How do I change the technician's color or name?** Color: **Admin → Schedule → Templates**. Name: their user account in **Admin → Company settings → Users**.

## Schedule customer notifications and appointment reminders

Granite Manager can text or email customers about their appointments and remind sales reps automatically. There are two systems:

1. **Customer notifications** that an admin sets up per calendar in **Admin → Schedule** (for example *1 day before every installation, remind the customer to disconnect the sink*).
2. **Built-in estimate messages** that come with **Schedule an Estimate** on a deal: a booking confirmation, customer reminders 24 hours and 1 hour before, and reminders to the sales rep.

---

### Customer notifications (Admin → Schedule)

**Where:** switch the sidebar to **Admin** → **Schedule** → **Customer notifications** card. The card starts collapsed; click its title to open it (this browser remembers). Inside are four tabs: **Reminders (N)**, **Confirmations (N)**, **Flows (N)** and **On my way**. Only users with **Admin** access can set them up.

The card reads *Texts and emails sent to the customer before and after appointments that have a customer picked. Write reminders, then put them in a flow for a calendar. The calendar's default flow goes on every new event; any event can swap it for other flows. Confirmations are sent by hand from the event.* (just *Emails…* when the company has no texting).

**The two kinds of templates:**

| Kind | Tab | How it is sent |
|------|-----|----------------|
| **Reminder** | **Reminders** | *Goes in flows, sent at a time before or after the appointment.* Flows send it automatically (for example *1 day before: disconnect the sink*). |
| **Confirmation** | **Confirmations** | *Employees send it by hand with "Send a confirmation now"* on the event (for example *Your installation is confirmed*). Never sent by a flow. |

#### 1. Add a reminder or a confirmation

1. Open the **Reminders** or **Confirmations** tab and click **Add reminder** or **Add confirmation**.
2. In **New reminder** / **New confirmation**: the **Reminder** / **Confirmation** switch at the top (a template a flow uses stays a reminder: *A flow sends it, so it stays a reminder.*), **Name** (for example *Disconnect the sink*), **Text** or **Email** (the choice shows only when the company can text; otherwise templates are emails), the **Subject** (email) and the **Message**. A new template starts with a ready text (*Hi {{customer.first_name}}, this is a reminder of your appointment with {{company.name}} on {{appointment.date}} at {{appointment.time}}.*, or *…is confirmed for…*). Texts show a counter up to 1600 characters (*Texts must be 1600 characters or less.*).
3. Click **Add**.

Empty tabs say *No reminders yet. Add one, e.g. a reminder to disconnect the sink.* and *No confirmations yet. Add one, e.g. "Your installation is confirmed".*

#### 2. Add a flow

1. Under **Flows**, click **Add flow** (it needs at least one reminder and one calendar: *Add a reminder first, then put it in a flow.*). Only reminders can go in a flow.
2. In **New flow** (an existing one opens as **Edit flow**) fill in **Name** (for example *Installation reminders*) and **Appointments on** (the calendar).
3. Under **Templates and when each goes out (sent in time order)**, pick a template and when it goes out: a number, **minutes**, **hours** or **days**, and **before** the appointment or **after** it ends. With days, also choose the time of day (**at the appointment time** / **at the time it ends**, or a clock time from 7:00 AM to 8:00 PM). **Add template to the flow** adds another step (up to 10, each from 1 minute up to 30 days).
4. **Default for <calendar>** — on: the flow is *Added to every new event on this calendar*; off: people pick it when they make an event. A calendar has one default flow.
5. **On** — off keeps the flow but sends nothing.
6. Click **Add**.

For the **Estimates** calendar the dialog warns: *Booked estimates already get built-in reminders 24 hours and 1 hour before. An estimate with one of your flows sending before it gets only your reminders.*

#### Variables

Click **Insert Variable** above the message to insert a placeholder at the cursor. They are filled in when each message is sent:

- **Appointment:** *Appointment date* (e.g. *Tuesday, January 15*), *Start time* (e.g. *10:00 AM*, or *All day*), *Appointment address* (the event's **Location**).
- **Customer:** first name, last name, full name, email, phone, address, inventory page.
- **Employee:** first, last and full name, email, phone number — this is the customer's sales rep (or, without one, whoever created the event).
- **Company:** name, address, hours of operation.
- **Date:** current day and month.

*If one cannot be filled (e.g. the appointment has no address), that customer is not sent this message.*

#### Edit, pause or delete

- Click a template or flow (or its pencil, **Edit**) to change it, then **Save**. Editing a template changes what its flows send from then on.
- Use a flow's switch to turn it off or on without losing it. **Make default** makes a flow its calendar's default.
- The trash (**Delete**) asks **Delete this flow?** — *Customers stop getting it. To pause it instead, turn it off.* A template used by a flow has to be taken out of the flow before it can be deleted.

#### On my way message

The **On my way** tab holds the message a customer gets when the installer or template technician taps **On my way** on their own schedule (*Texted to the customer when the installer or template technician taps On my way on their schedule. Nothing is sent until you write it.*).

1. Open the **On my way** tab.
2. Write the **Message**; the grey example shows one (*Hi {{customer.first_name}}, this is {{company.name}}. Our crew is on the way to {{appointment.address}}.*). **Insert Variable** adds the same variables as templates. Texts show a counter up to 1600 characters.
3. Without texting it goes by email: fill in the **Subject** too (empty uses *On the way*).
4. Click **Save**; **Saved** confirms it. Emptying the message and saving turns it off.

It goes by text from the Office Manager's line when the company can text, otherwise by email, to the event's own phone or email, else the customer's. It goes out once per job. When it can't go (no message set up, no linked customer, no phone or email, no Office Manager line, a variable that can't be filled), the job is still marked On my way and the crew's toast says why. Each tap is written to the event's history (*On my way: the customer got a text*, *On my way (no message: …)*).

#### On one event (the event's Notifications)

When you create or edit an event, the **Notifications** box shows the flows it will send: the calendar's default flow is already there. Click **Remove** (the X) to turn a flow off for this event, or **Add notifications** to add another flow. With none: *The customer gets no notifications for this event.* **Send a confirmation now** (*Goes to the customer as soon as you save.*) lists the company's **Confirmation** templates: switch it on, tick the ones to send (a text and an email to send both) and save. Toast **Confirmation sent** (*The customer got it by text / email*) or **Confirmation not sent** with the reason. Without confirmation templates: *No confirmation templates yet. Admins add them in Admin > Schedule.*

#### Who receives it, and from where

- **The customer:** the customer picked in the event's **Customer** box (or the customer of the sale the event belongs to). Events with only a typed name get nothing.
- **Texts** go to the customer's phone from the line of the user with the **Office Manager** position who has a texting line set up. Without such an Office Manager, texts are not sent.
- **Emails** go to the customer's primary email, from their sales rep's email (or the event creator's).
- Times in messages are the store's time.

#### When a message is sent, or skipped

- Each step of a flow goes out once per appointment when its time arrives. Steps **after** count from the appointment's end.
- If the event is moved to a new date or time, the messages are timed again for the new time.
- Not sent when: the event has no linked customer; the event repeats; the send time had already passed when the event was booked (or when the step was added); a variable can't be filled; the customer has no phone (texts) or no email (emails); there is no Office Manager line (texts); or, for a step before the appointment, the appointment has already started. Turned-off flows, flows removed from the event and deleted events send nothing.
- An event with one of your flows on no longer gets the built-in estimate reminders (see the note below).

---

### Booking an in-home estimate (Schedule an Estimate)

**Where:** open a deal (**CRM → Deals**) → **Project** tab → **Schedule an Estimate** (next to the won/lost buttons). Available to employees. It books on the calendar an admin picks in **Admin > Schedule** → **Schedule estimate** (the **Estimates** calendar until another is picked).

1. Click **Schedule an Estimate**. The dialog shows the customer, their email and phone, and their address (map button **Open in Google Maps**).
2. **Starts** / **Ends** default to tomorrow 12:00–1:00 PM. While *Checking the conversation for an agreed time…* shows, the app reads the customer's recent texts and emails; if they agreed on a time it fills it in and shows *Time from the conversation: "…". Check it before submitting.*
3. Adjust the times and click **Submit**.

The customer needs a phone number or email; otherwise **Submit** stays disabled with *Add a phone number or email so the customer can receive the appointment confirmation.*

What happens automatically:

- The estimate is added to that calendar with the customer's name as its title, their address as the location and their email and phone in the description.
- **Confirmation to the customer:** a text from the Office Manager's line (company texting set up, Office Manager line, customer phone), otherwise an email from the customer's sales rep (or from you). The toast **Estimate scheduled** says which: *…was added to <calendar> and notified by text…* / *…by email…*, or *The estimate was saved, but we could not send a confirmation by text or email.* The text reads like *Hi Alice, your in-home estimate with Rita is scheduled for Tuesday, January 15 at 10:00 AM – 11:00 AM. Contact Rita at 317-555-0100. Address: 1 Main St.* Emails use the subject *[Company] - In-Home Estimate Scheduled*.
- **Customer reminders:** 24 hours before (*…this is a reminder that your in-home estimate with … is scheduled for …*, email subject *[Company] - In-Home Estimate Reminder*) and 1 hour before (*…starts in about 1 hour…*, subject *[Company] - In-Home Estimate Starting Soon*). Same channel rules as the confirmation. A reminder whose time has already passed when booking is skipped.
- **Sales rep reminders:** the customer's sales rep (or whoever booked it) gets an entry in **Notifications** (the bell) and a Telegram message, if Telegram is connected, at 5 PM store time the day before (*In-home estimate tomorrow with …*) and 1 hour before (*In-home estimate in 1 hour with …*). These need a deal: the deal it was booked from, or the customer's newest deal.
- Moving the estimate (editing its dates, or a route rebuild) re-times all these reminders; deleting it cancels them.

**Note:** an estimate with one of the company's flows sending before it gets only those reminders, not the built-in 24-hour and 1-hour ones (the flow form warns about this). Because **Schedule an Estimate** saves the customer's name as plain text, a company flow only reaches that estimate after someone edits the event and picks the customer in the **Customer** box. Sales rep reminders are not affected.

Installations and template appointments do not get built-in customer reminders; set up a flow for those calendars if customers should be reminded.

### Common questions

- **Can the customer get the confirmation by text and by email?** Yes: when you create or edit the event, tick a text and an email template under **Send a confirmation now** in its **Notifications** box, then save.
- **Why didn't the customer get a reminder?** It isn't sent when the event has no linked customer (a typed name gets nothing), the event repeats, the send time had already passed when it was booked, or a variable can't be filled. Texts also need a user with the **Office Manager** position who has a texting line.
- **The customer got no reminder.** Check: the event's **Customer** was picked from the search (not typed); the event doesn't repeat; the flow is **On** and on the event (its **Notifications** box); the customer has a phone (texts) or email (emails); for texts, an **Office Manager** has a texting line; the message's variables can all be filled (for example the event has a **Location** if the message uses the address); and the appointment was booked before the send time.
- **I don't see the Text option.** The company has no texting set up, so only email templates are available.
- **Can a customer get two reminders?** Yes: every step of the event's flows is sent (for example 1 day before and 2 hours before).
- **How do I stop the reminders for one customer's appointment?** Open the event, remove the flow in its **Notifications** box and save.
- **How do I turn customer reminders off?** **Admin > Schedule** → **Customer notifications** → switch the flow off (or delete it).
- **Who are texts signed by?** Whatever the message says; use variables like *Company name* or *Employee full name*. They are sent from the Office Manager's line.
- **Where do sales rep reminders show?** In the **Notifications** bell in the app header and in Telegram (connect it on **My Account**).
- **Schedule an Estimate is disabled.** The calendar it books on wasn't found; reload the page, or ask an admin to pick one in **Admin > Schedule** → **Schedule estimate**.

## Schedule (company calendar)

The **Schedule** is the company calendar for templating (measuring) appointments, installations, in-home estimates and any other calendars your company adds. Everyone in the office sees the same events, can filter them by calendar and by installer or templater, search them, open them to comment, and build a driving route for a day.

**Where to find it:** Employee sidebar → **Schedule** (a top-level item with a calendar icon, below the sidebar sections). It opens on the **Month** view of the current month (`/employee/schedule/month`).

**Who can use it:** every user with **Employee** access (sales reps, sales managers, office managers, managers, Super Admins). Admins open it from the Employee view (switch to **Employee** in the sidebar header). In the **Admin** sidebar, **Schedule** is a different page: the schedule settings (installer and template colors, calendars, customer notifications). See *Admin Schedule settings* and *Schedule customer notifications*.

**Who uses something else:** installers (Installer position) and template technicians (Template Guy position) are locked into their own phone-friendly portals that show only the jobs assigned to them. See *Installer portal & checklists* and *My Schedule / template portal*.

Related: creating, editing, copying and deleting events are described in *Schedule events: create, edit, copy, delete*.

---

### Calendars on the schedule

Every company has three built-in calendars that cannot be renamed or deleted:

| Calendar | Used for |
|----------|----------|
| **Templates** | Templating / measuring appointments. Events can be assigned to a **Template** person (users with the Template Guy position). |
| **Installations** | Installation jobs. Events can be assigned to an **Installer** (users with the Installer position). With QuickBooks connected, an installation can also show a QuickBooks invoice. |
| **Estimates** | In-home estimates. **Schedule an Estimate** on a deal puts the appointment here and confirms it with the customer. |

Admins can add more calendars (for example *Service calls*), turn calendars off, and hide a calendar from specific people in **Admin → Schedule**. A calendar hidden from you does not appear in your **Calendars** list or in the event form.

---

### Page layout

- **Left panel (desktop and tablet):** **View** (**Month**, **Week**, **Day**), **Calendars** (**All calendars** plus each calendar), when the Installations or Templates calendar is picked the **Installers** or **Templaters** filter, and **Unscheduled**: jobs that have no date yet. It shows three at a time (**Show N more** / **Show less**), with a **Search** box (title, customer, address or calendar) and a sort button (**Oldest first**, **Newest first**, **Name A–Z**, **Ready first**). Click a job to open its **Event details** (edit from there).
- **On phones:** the left panel is hidden. Tap the round sliders button next to the title (**View and calendars**) to open the same panel. A large round **+** button at the bottom right adds an event.
- **Top bar:** the title (month, week range or full date), a small round **+** button (**Add event**, desktop), the **Search events…** box, and **Prev** / **Next**.

---

### Views

#### Month

- A grid of weeks that start on Sunday, or on Monday when an admin picks that in **Admin → Schedule**. Sundays are shown in red; today's date is in a black circle. A few days of the previous and next month fill the first and last rows (greyed).
- **All-day events** show as solid colored bars. **Timed events** show a colored dot and the title; when the day cells are wide enough the start time shows too. On narrow screens (or with the event panel open) timed events become tinted chips.
- When a day has more events than fit, the last row reads **+N more** (desktop; *View all events*). On phones a small grey triangle appears in the top-right corner of the day instead. Both open the day list.
- Click the month name to open **Choose month and year**: arrows change the year, then pick a month.
- Click an empty part of a day to create an all-day event on that day. Click the date number of a day that has events (tooltip *View this day's route*) to open the day list.

#### Week

- Seven days from the company's first day of the week (Sunday or Monday) with an hour grid. Click any hour slot to create a one-hour event starting then.
- The first two all-day events of each day are listed under its date. On phones the date shows a count such as *3 events*.
- Moving the mouse over the grid shows a red time line with the time.

#### Day

- A full-date title, the day's route map (when the events' addresses can be placed on a map, else *No stops with an address*) with a **Google Maps** link, and the hour grid. Click an hour slot to create a one-hour event.
- The Week and Day hour grids show **timed** events. To see all-day events of a day, use Month view or the day list.

**What an event shows as its title:** its own **Title**. Linking a customer fills in the customer's name, which can then be changed.

Each card shows the event's title and dates, the assigned person's (or creator's) initials and its latest history lines with their times (*Date updated*, *Notes updated*, comments…). - **Week starts on** — **Sunday** or **Monday**: the first day of each week in the month and week views, the event form's date pickers and your own schedule. Until you pick one, you get the company's choice (Admin > Schedule).

### Filtering by calendar

In **Calendars** (left panel, or **View and calendars** on phones):

1. **All calendars** shows every calendar.
2. Click a calendar's name to show **only** that calendar.
3. Use the **–** / **+** button on a calendar's row (**Remove from current view** / **Add to current view**) to combine several calendars.

The **Installers** filter appears only while the **Installations** calendar is picked (not with **All calendars**); the **Templaters** filter appears while **Templates** is picked.

1. **All installers** (or **All templaters**) shows everyone.
2. Click a person's name (with their color dot) to show only their events.
3. Use **–** / **+** on a row to add or remove people.

While anyone is picked, events on that calendar with **no** person assigned are hidden too. The filter only narrows its own calendar; events on other calendars stay visible. The same filter appears as chips at the top of the day list.

### Searching events

1. Type in **Search events…** (on phones in Month view, tap the magnifier **Search events** first).
2. Results match the event title, the linked customer's name, the address, the description and the note, across all dates. Each result shows the date and time and the address.
3. Five results show first; **Show N more** shows the rest (up to 25). None: *No events found* · *Try another title or keyword*.
4. Click a result: the schedule jumps to that date and opens the event.

*No events found* means nothing matched; try another name, street or keyword.

### The day list (Month view)

Open it by clicking a day's date number (when it has events) or **+N more**. The dialog is titled with the full date and contains:

- **Add** — creates an all-day event on that day.
- The **Installers** / **Templaters** chips (when that calendar is picked).
- Route buttons and the day's map with a **Google Maps** link (see below).
- One row per event: a color bar, the title, the assigned installer or template person (or else the person who created the event), the time (**All day** or a time range) and the address. Clicking the address opens Google Maps directions; the copy icon (**Copy address**) copies it.
- Row buttons: **Copy event**, **Edit event**, **Delete event**.
- Clicking a row opens its **Event details** beside the list (on phones the list closes).

*No events scheduled for this day* shows when the filters leave nothing.

### Building a day's route

Routes are built **per installer** from the events that have an address.

1. Open the day list for the date.
2. Click **Route: *installer name* (N stops)**. Events with no person assigned are grouped under **No installer**. A button is disabled until it has at least two stops (*Needs at least 2 events with an address*); a route can have at most 20 stops.
3. If two or more of the stops are one-time events with set times, a confirmation **Build route: *name*** explains that those times will be swapped to follow the route. Click **Build and reschedule** (or **Cancel**).
4. The toast **Route built** confirms it. The stops are ordered by the fastest drive from the company address.

What changes:

- Timed, one-time events trade their existing start times: the first stop on the route gets the earliest time, and each event keeps its own length. Each moved event gets the history line *Time changed by route optimization*, and its appointment reminders are re-timed.
- All-day events keep their day and are only reordered; the order is remembered in this browser for that day.
- Repeating events are ordered but keep their times.

The route starts from the company address, so it must be filled in (**Admin → Company settings → Company**). Without it the error reads *Add the company address in settings so the route has a starting point.*

---

### Auto-plan (installations and templates)

Auto-plan gives the waiting jobs of one installer or templater a day and a time, fitted around that person's schedule.

1. In the left panel pick the **Installations** (or **Templates**) calendar, then exactly one person in the **Installers** (or **Templaters**) filter.
2. Under **Unscheduled**, pick the **Installations** (or **Templates**) tab when there are several. The calendar-clock button (**Auto-plan**, *Auto-plan unscheduled jobs*) appears next to **+** (**Add unscheduled customer**: *Add a customer with no date yet*). It does not show for **All**, other calendars or several people. When the company has nobody in that role, it plans for the calendar's unassigned jobs.
3. Choose **Starting** (tomorrow by default), how many **Work days** to fill (1 to 30) and the statuses to plan (**Ready** by default; **Called** and **Not ready** too if you want).
4. Click **Plan**. Nothing is saved yet (*No jobs to plan.* when there are none). Each proposed job shows its time, length, drive time and address, grouped by day; *Not planned* lists jobs left out and why.
5. Untick any job you don't want, then click **Schedule N jobs** (**Schedule 1 job** for one; toast *N jobs scheduled* or *1 job scheduled*). The jobs leave **Unscheduled**, go on the calendar at those times and are assigned to that person, in their color.

How the plan is made:

- Jobs are the person's own waiting jobs and the unassigned ones on that calendar, oldest first.
- A job's length comes from its sale and **Admin → Schedule → Job time**. Without a sale, the event's own length is used; with neither, it is skipped (*No sale to size it from, and the event has no length.*).
- The person's other events that day, on any calendar, are kept free. An all-day event blocks the day.
- The day starts at the shop (**Work day from**). It opens with the oldest waiting job; after that the job that can start soonest, which is the nearest by Google drive time, goes next, until nothing more fits before the end of the work day. The drive to the next stop is kept free too.
- Drive times come from Google Maps between the company address and the jobs' addresses, for up to 20 addresses. Without an address the **Drive time without an address** minutes are used, and a note says why.
- A job longer than a work day fills a free day and is marked *Longer than a work day: it fills the day. Check the sale.*

### Event details panel

Clicking an event opens **Event details** on the right (full screen on phones). **Escape** closes it.

- **⋮ (More options)** → **Edit**, **Copy**, **Delete**.
- At the top: the creator's initials (hover: *Created by …*) and the title. Once the crew has started the job, a tag shows their status and its time: *On my way · 9:42 AM* (blue), *Arrived · 10:05 AM* (amber) or *Completed · 1:30 PM* (green), from the **On my way** and **Completed** buttons on their own schedule. With location on in the Granite Phone app, the crew's phone also sets them by itself: reaching the job's address marks it **Arrived**, and driving about half a mile away from the shop or the job they were at marks their next job **On my way** (without sending the customer the On my way message). Only the **Completed** button completes a job. Moving a job to another day clears its statuses.
- **Start → End** date and time (or **All day**).
- The description and note, the calendar, the assigned installer or template person (or *No installer assigned* / *No template assigned*), for an event linked to a customer one line each for the customer's name, phone and email (click either to copy) and **Sales rep**, the address (opens Google Maps directions), the QuickBooks invoice with **View PDF** (when QuickBooks is connected), and the attachments.
- **Activity feed:** comments, files added to comments and history lines (*Event created*, *Date updated*, *Label updated*, *Location updated*, *Title changed to …*, *Notes updated*, *Calendar changed*, *Repeat updated*, *Attachment added*, *On my way: the customer got a text*, *Completed*…), grouped by date. Moving a job to another day clears the crew's status.
- **Comment box** at the bottom: type in **Comment** and press Enter or the send button (**Send comment**). The paperclip (**Add file to comment**) attaches photos or documents. Your own comments have a menu (**Comment actions**) with **Edit** and **Delete**; your own files have one (**File actions**) with **Delete**. Each asks to confirm: **Delete this comment?** (*This comment will be removed.*) or **Delete this file?** (*This file will be removed from the comments.*).
- Right-hand buttons: **Attachments** (files added in the event form), **People** (**Creator** and **Assigned**; *No people linked to this event* when there are none) and **History**. An event with no project shows *No project for this event.* in its project part.

## Shop Maintenance (`/shop/maintenance`)

**Maintenance** tracks the shop's equipment (saw, CNC, polisher, forklift, truck…) and the service checks each one needs (change oil, replace blade, grease bearings…). Each check comes due after a number of **days**, a number of **hours** (or **miles**) of use, or whichever comes first. The page shows what is **OK**, what to **Check today**, and what is **Overdue**, and keeps a history of who did each check.

**Page title:** **Maintenance** — *Equipment and service checks for the shop.*

---

### Where to find it and who can do what

| Who | Where | What they can do |
|-----|-------|------------------|
| **Shop Worker** | Shop sidebar → **Maintenance** | View equipment and checks, **Done** (mark a check completed), **History**, update hours/miles used |
| **Shop Manager** | Employee or Admin sidebar → **Maintenance** (top-level item). Opening it switches to the shop sidebar (**Transactions**, **Samples**, **Maintenance**, **My Account**) | Everything above, plus **Edit mode**: add, edit and delete equipment and checks |
| Other staff | No sidebar link | — |

Only users with the **Shop Manager** position see the **Edit mode** button. Positions are set by a Manager in **Admin > Company settings > Users**.

---

### Reading the page

Equipment shows as cards, worst status first, then the soonest due date, then by name. Each card has:

- A colored dot: **green = OK**, **amber = Check today** (a check is due today), **red = Overdue** (a due date has passed). The card takes the worst status of its checks.
- The equipment **name** and **N checks**.
- **Total hours of work [n]** (or **Total miles [n]**) — the current meter reading, when set.
- **Next due [date]** — the earliest due date among its checks.

Empty page: *No equipment yet.* (Shop Managers: *No equipment yet. Turn on Edit mode to add items like Saw.*)

Click a card to open its **equipment dialog**:

- Title = equipment name, with its usage line, e.g. `8 h/day · 20 days/month · Total hours of work 1250` (or *Set usage hours on the equipment to enable hours-based checks.*).
- One box per check: status dot, **check name**, its usage line, and its conditions:
  - Days condition: **Every 90 days** — **Due [date]**.
  - Hours condition: **Every 100 hours · 35/100 h done** — **Due [date]** (miles: `mi`). Click this box to update the hours used.
- Buttons per check: **History**, **Done** (and **Edit** / **Delete** in Edit mode).
- *No checks yet.* when the equipment has none. **Close** at the bottom.

#### How due dates are worked out

- **Days condition:** due that many days after the check was last completed (or created/saved).
- **Hours/Miles condition:** remaining hours ÷ average daily use, counted from today. Average daily use = **Hours / day** × **Days / month** ÷ 30 (taken from the check if it has its own numbers, otherwise from the equipment). Hour-based checks need both numbers set.
- **Either condition due means the check is due. Completing resets both.**

---

### Everyday use (all shop users)

#### Marking a check done

1. Click the equipment card, then **Done** on the check.
2. Dialog **Mark completed** — *Completing [check] resets all conditions.*
3. If the check has an hours/miles condition, enter **Total hours of work** (or **Total miles**) — the current hour meter / odometer reading (required, pre-filled with the last saved reading when there is one). It is saved into the completion notes and becomes the new starting reading.
4. Optional **Notes** (*What was done…*).
5. Click **Mark completed**. Toast: **Marked as completed**.

Every condition of the check starts over from today, and the status turns green.

If you see *Set hours/day and days/month on this check or on the equipment before completing hour-based checks*, a Shop Manager must fill in those numbers first.

#### Updating hours (or miles) used

Use this between services so the due date stays accurate.

1. Open the equipment and click the check's **Every … hours** box.
2. Dialog **Update hours** (or **Update miles**) — *Hours done since last reset (of 100). Due date updates from remaining hours.*
3. Type the hours used since the last completion and click **Save**. Toast: **Hours updated**.

Only hour/mile conditions can be updated this way. The value can't be negative and stops counting at the interval.

#### Viewing history

Click **History** on a check. **Completion history** lists each completion, newest first: date and time (`MM/dd/yy · h:mm a`, or *Unknown date* when none was saved), **Completed by [name]**, and the notes (including the meter reading), or *No notes*. *No completions yet.* if it was never done. **Close** to go back.

---

### Setting up equipment and checks (Shop Manager)

Click **Edit mode** (top right). It changes to **Done editing**; **Add equipment** appears, and cards and checks get **Edit** / **Delete** buttons.

#### Adding or editing equipment

1. **Add equipment** (or **Edit** on a card).
2. Dialog **Add equipment** / **Edit equipment**:
   - **Name** (required, e.g. *Saw*).
   - **Hours / day** (or **Miles / day**) — typical use per working day (hours: max 24).
   - **Days / month** — working days per month (max 31).
   - **Starting hours (optional)** / **Starting miles (optional)** — meter reading when you start tracking — with the **Hours / Miles** unit selector.
   - *Used to estimate due dates for hours-based checks.*
3. Click **Create** (or **Save**). Toasts: **Equipment added**, **Equipment updated**.

#### Adding or editing a check

1. In Edit mode open the equipment card → **Add check** (or **Edit** on a check).
2. Dialog **Add check** / **Edit check** (*For [equipment]*):
   - **Name** (required, e.g. *Change oil*) and **Notes**.
   - **Hours for this check** box (optional; it reads **Miles for this check** when the equipment's **Meter unit** is miles): **Hours / day**, **Days / month**, **Starting hours (optional)** + unit. *Leave blank to use [equipment] hours.* Fill these only when this part is used differently from the machine.
   - **Hours condition** (or **Miles condition**) checkbox + interval (default 100).
   - **Days condition** checkbox + interval (default 90).
   - At least one condition is required (**Create** stays disabled otherwise).
3. Click **Create** / **Save**. Toasts: **Check added**, **Check updated**.

Saving a check restarts its conditions from today (hours used go back to 0). An hours condition on equipment without **Hours / day** and **Days / month** fails with *Could not calculate due date*.

#### Deleting

- **Delete** on a check → confirm dialog *Are you sure you want to delete [check]?* → **Confirm**. Toast **Check deleted**.
- **Delete** on an equipment card → **Confirm**. Toast **Equipment deleted**. Its checks and conditions are deleted too.

Click **Done editing** when finished.

---

### Reminders

Every day around **9 AM** (store time), each **Shop Worker** and **Shop Manager** who has connected **Telegram** on **My Account** gets a Telegram message **Maintenance due today** listing the checks due that day (`Equipment · Check`) and a link to this page. It is sent once per day and only lists checks due **today** — overdue checks are not repeated, so check the page for red items. No email is sent.

---

### Common questions / troubleshooting

- **I don't see Edit mode / Add equipment.** Only the **Shop Manager** position can edit. Shop Workers can mark checks done and update hours.
- **I don't see Maintenance in my sidebar.** It shows in the shop sidebar and, for **Shop Managers**, in the Employee/Admin sidebar.
- **The hours condition has no due date / I can't complete it.** Set **Hours / day** and **Days / month** on the equipment (or on the check).
- **The due date jumped after I edited the check.** Saving a check restarts its conditions from today.
- **How do I record miles instead of hours?** Choose **Miles** in the unit selector next to the starting reading.
- **I didn't get the Telegram reminder.** Reminders go to Shop Workers and Shop Managers with Telegram connected, only for checks due that day.
- **Can I undo a completion?** No. Mark it done again later or ask a Shop Manager to adjust the check.
- **A "sample" machine appeared.** It is a demo for the guided tour; changes to it are not saved.

## Shop portal (`/shop`)

The **shop portal** is the simple app for the fabrication floor. Shop staff use it to see which sold jobs need cutting, record cuts and leftovers, keep sample counts, and look after equipment maintenance. It does not include customers, deals, quotes or selling.

---

### Who uses it

| Position | How they get here | What they can open |
|----------|-------------------|--------------------|
| **Shop Worker** | Signing in opens **Transactions** (`/shop/transactions`) automatically | Only the shop portal: **Transactions**, **Samples**, **Maintenance**, **Schedule**, **My Account** (and **Shop Statistic** by its address). They cannot open the Employee CRM or Admin |
| **Shop Manager** | From the Employee or Admin sidebar → **Maintenance**; the sidebar then switches to the shop sidebar | The shop pages plus their normal Employee/Admin pages. Only Shop Managers can edit equipment in **Maintenance** |

- A user can't be both **Sales Representative** and **Shop Worker** (turning one on in the user editor turns the other off).
- If a user also has **Installer**, **Walk-in** or **Marketing**, that portal wins and they land there instead.
- Positions are changed by a Manager with Admin access in **Admin > Company settings > Users**.

Opening `/shop` by itself goes to **Transactions**.

---

### Shop sidebar

| Item | What it's for | Details in |
|------|---------------|-----------|
| **Transactions** | Sold jobs to cut. Filter by **Sales Rep** / **Status**, open a job, mark slabs **Cut** / **Uncut**, record leftovers (**Partial**), **Replace**, **Remove**, **Add Slab**, add rooms, fix room square feet | **Shop Worker — Transactions** |
| **Samples** | Sample count per stone: **Amount** (type a number or use **−** to take one off), **Importance** (**High**, **Medium**, **Low**, **Hadn't cut**), stone search, **Out of stock** button to sort stones running low on samples to the top | **Samples & Special Order calculator** |
| **Schedule** | The company schedule (installs, templates and other calendars), the same Month, Week and Day views as the Employee **Schedule** | **Schedule** |
| **Maintenance** | Equipment and service checks: **OK** / **Check today** / **Overdue**, **Done** (mark completed), **History**, update hours or miles; Shop Managers use **Edit mode** to add equipment and checks | **Shop Maintenance** |
| **My Account** | Your profile and Telegram | below |

The sidebar footer has the **Chat** assistant, as in the rest of the app. On phones, the Employee/Admin/Customer switch buttons are not shown in the shop sidebar.

---

### What shop staff do (typical day)

1. Sign in — **Transactions** opens with **Status: In Progress**.
2. Open a job, work room by room: **Cut** fully used slabs; **Partial** when a usable remnant is left (enter leftover **Length** × **Width**); **Replace** if you must use another bundle of the same stone.
3. When every slab is cut, the job shows **Cut**. Office staff then mark it installed from Employee **Transactions** (**⋯** → **Mark as Installed**) — shop users can't.
4. Check **Maintenance** for red (**Overdue**) or amber (**Check today**) equipment; click **Done** after servicing.
5. Update **Samples** counts when samples are taken or cut.

Shop staff can't sell slabs, change prices, customers or sinks, or cancel a sale — sales reps do that from **Inventory > Stones**.

### My Account (shop)

Shop sidebar → **My Account**. Page title **My Account**.

- **Telegram** — *Connect the notifications bot to get maintenance and shop alerts in Telegram.* Click **Connect notifications bot** and finish in Telegram; the section then shows **Done**. Shop Workers and Shop Managers with Telegram connected get the daily **Maintenance due today** message (see **Shop Maintenance**). More in **My Account & Telegram**.
- **Personal Information** — **Name** (required), **Phone** (at least 10 digits), **Email**, **Password** (*Leave empty to keep current password*; at least 8 characters).
- **Save Changes** — toast **Your account was updated**. Errors show under the form (*We couldn't save that. Please try again*).
- **Logout** button (red, next to **Save Changes**).
- While the guided tour is active you may also see *Learning progress — N points* and the onboarding checklist.

### Shop Statistic (`/shop/statistics`)

A page of how much the shop cut. It is **not in the sidebar** — open it by typing the address. Shop Workers and employees can open it. Page title **Shop Statistic**.

- **Start date** / **End date** — default is the last 30 days up to today. Pick dates to change the range.
- **Materials cut (sqft)** — square feet cut per material (stone type, e.g. granite, quartz; **Unknown** when the stone has no type) and a **Total**.
- **Sqft cut per day** — bar chart.
- **Cut days** — a card per day with total square feet and the breakdown by material. *No data for selected dates* when nothing was cut.

What counts: sold slabs in **rooms where every slab is cut**, on the day each slab was cut. A slab's square feet come from the room square feet on the sale, or length × width ÷ 144 when not set. Rooms that still have an uncut slab are left out until they are finished.

## Shop Worker — Transactions (`/shop/transactions`)

Use **Transactions** in the shop portal to find sales that need fabrication, open a job, and record the work on its slabs: **Cut**, **Uncut**, **Partial** (record leftover pieces), **Replace**, **Remove**, add slabs and rooms, and correct each room's square feet.

**Where to find it:** shop portal sidebar → **Transactions**. The page title is **Sales Transactions**.

**Who can see it:**

- **Shop Worker** position — signing in opens this page. Shop Workers are kept inside the shop portal: they can open only **Transactions**, **Samples**, **Maintenance**, and **My Account**, never the employee CRM or Admin. (If the same user also holds **Installer**, **Walk-in**, or **Marketing**, that portal wins instead. Super Admins and platform superusers are never locked to a portal.)
- **Shop Manager** position — the Employee and Admin sidebars show **Maintenance**. Opening it switches to the shop sidebar, where **Transactions** is also available.
- Sales reps, office staff, and admins use **Transactions** in their own Employee or Admin sidebar instead — see **Transactions — Employee & Admin**.

A user cannot be both **Sales Representative** and **Shop Worker**; turning one on in the user editor turns the other off.

---

### The transaction list

#### Filters (top left)

| Filter | Options | Default |
|--------|---------|---------|
| **Sales Rep** | **All**, or one seller (everyone who has sold something in your company) | **All** |
| **Status** | **In Progress**, **Finished**, **All Statuses** | **In Progress** |

- **In Progress** — not installed and not cancelled.
- **Finished** — installed or cancelled.
- **All Statuses** — everything.

Your filter choices stay in the page address, so they are kept when you open and close a transaction.

#### Search (top right)

- Box placeholder: **Search transactions...**
- Matches customer name, seller, bundle, or stone name, within the sales the current filters show.
- A dropdown lists up to 20 matches with customer name, sale date, seller, and project address (**No address** when none). Click a match to open it.
- Sales with no slabs are left out of search results.

#### Table columns

Every column can be sorted by clicking its header.

| Column | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| **Date** | Sale date |
| **Customer** | Customer name (blue) |
| **Sold By** | Seller |
| **Stone** | Stone name(s) on the sale. Red and struck through = that slab was deleted from inventory. |
| **Sqft** | Square feet of the sale — each room's square feet added up (**N/A** when none) |
| **Sink** | Sink models on the sale; repeats show a count, e.g. `[model] x 2` (**N/A** when none) |

| **Status** | See below |

| Status | Color | Meaning |

| **Sold** | Green | No slab cut yet |
| **Partially Cut** | Gray | At least one slab cut, not all |
| **Cut** | Blue | Every slab on the sale is cut |

| **Cancelled** | Red | The sale was cancelled (unsold) |

**Open a transaction:** click any row, or a search result. The **Transaction Details** dialog opens over the list.

### Transaction Details dialog

#### Top cards (read-only)

- **Sale Information** — **Customer**, **Sale Date**, **Sold By**, **Project Address** (**No address** when empty).
- **Room Sinks** — sink models grouped by room, with a count such as `x2` when a room has several of the same model. Shows **No sinks** when there are none. Sinks cannot be changed here.

#### Rooms card

Slabs are grouped by **room** (Kitchen, Bathroom, etc.). Each room shows:

- **Room name** in the header.
- **Total sqft per room:** — the room's square feet, with a pencil to edit it (see below).
- A table: **Bundle**, **Stone**, **Status**, **Notes**, **Cut Date**, **Actions**.
  - **Stone** shows **(Partial)** after the name when the slab is a leftover piece of another slab, or when pieces have been recorded from it.
  - **Status** badge: **Uncut** (green) or **Cut** (blue).
  - **Notes** — the notes saved with that slab on the sale; hover to read long notes. **-** when none.
  - **Cut Date** — the date the slab was marked cut, or **-**.

If the sale has no slabs, the card shows **No slabs in this transaction**.

Buttons at the bottom of the dialog: **Add Slab** and **Close**.

#### Slab actions (the ⋯ menu, titled **Actions**)

| Action | Shown when | What it does |
|--------|------------|--------------|
| **Cut** | Slab is uncut | Marks the slab cut with today's date |
| **Uncut** | Slab is cut | Reverses the cut (for corrections) |
| **Partial** | Slab is uncut | Opens **Mark as partially cut** to record leftover pieces |
| **Replace** | Always listed | Swaps the slab for another free bundle of the same stone. Only works on uncut slabs. |
| **Remove** | Always listed | Takes the slab off this sale |

Success messages: **Slab marked as cut**, **Slab marked as uncut**, **Slab replaced**, **Slab removed from sale**, **Slab added to sale**. If something fails you see an **Error** message (for example **Could not update the sale**).

**Who can do these actions:** every action on this page — **Cut** / **Uncut** (which also add or clear leftover pieces), **Partial**, **Replace**, **Remove**, **Add Slab**, **Add Room** and editing room square feet — needs the **Shop Worker** or **Shop Manager** position (or Admin access). Other employees who reach this page get an error when they try. In the Employee sidebar **Transactions**, employees only have simple **Cut** / **Uncut**.

---

### Marking a slab cut

1. Open the transaction.
2. In the slab's row, click **⋯** → **Cut**.
3. Toast: **Slab marked as cut**. The badge turns blue (**Cut**) and **Cut Date** shows today.

**What happens:**

- Any **unsold leftover pieces** recorded for that slab are removed from inventory. If a usable leftover remains, use **Partial** instead of **Cut**.
- The sale's status updates automatically: **Partially Cut** while any slab is still uncut, **Cut** once every slab is cut.

**To undo:** **⋯** → **Uncut**. The slab goes back to **Uncut**, the cut date is cleared, and leftover sizes recorded for it are reset to the full slab size.

---

### Recording leftovers (Partial)

Use **Partial** when the slab is cut but a usable remnant is left.

1. In the slab's row, click **⋯** → **Partial**.
2. The **Mark as partially cut** dialog asks: *What are the leftover dimensions for slab [bundle]?*
3. Enter **Length** and **Width** of the leftover piece (both must be greater than zero, or nothing is saved).
4. Choose:
   - **More left overs** — saves this piece and clears the fields so you can enter another leftover piece from the same slab. The slab stays uncut.
   - **Done** — saves this piece, closes the dialog, and marks the slab **Cut**.

**Where the size is saved:** when the slab was sold as a partial slab (**Full Slab Sold** turned off when selling), it already has a leftover piece in inventory. The first size you enter updates that piece, and each **More left overs** adds another leftover piece of the same bundle. These pieces stay in inventory as remnants that sales reps can sell later. If the slab has no leftover piece, the size is recorded on the slab itself.

---

### Replacing a slab

Use **Replace** when the shop must use a different bundle of the same stone.

1. Make sure the slab is **Uncut**. On a cut slab, **Replace** shows **Uncut slab before replace** — use **Uncut** first.
2. Click **⋯** → **Replace**.
3. The **Replace Slab** dialog shows **Current slab [bundle]** and a list of free (unsold) bundles of the same stone, each labeled **Bundle [number]** with **Full** or **Partial**.
4. Click the bundle to use. The swap happens right away (no extra confirm). Toast: **Slab replaced**.

**What happens:** the new bundle takes the old slab's place in the same room, with its square feet, notes, and other sale details. The old slab returns to available inventory, and its unsold leftover pieces are removed.

**No available slabs** means every other bundle of that stone is sold. To switch to a different stone, use **Add Slab** and then **Remove** the old slab.

---

### Removing a slab from the sale

1. Click **⋯** → **Remove** on the slab.
2. The **Remove Slab** dialog asks: *Are you sure you want to remove slab [bundle] from this sale?*
3. Click **Delete** to confirm, or **Cancel**.
4. Toast: **Slab removed from sale**.

The slab goes back to available inventory with its room and sale details cleared, and its unsold leftover pieces are removed. You cannot remove the last slab on a sale — you see **Cannot remove last slab**.

---

### Adding a slab

1. Click **Add Slab** at the bottom of the dialog.
2. Under **Select room**, click the room the slab belongs to. (To use a new room, create it first with **Add Room** — see below.)
3. The dialog shows **Room: [name]** and a **Search stones** box, pre-filled with the first stone on the sale. Type to search; sold-out and hidden stones are included.
4. Click a stone on the left. Its free (unsold) bundles load on the right, each labeled **Bundle [number]** with **Full** or **Partial**.
5. Click a bundle. It is added right away. Toast: **Slab added to sale**.

The new slab is added **uncut** and takes the room's details (square feet, price, edge, and so on) from the first slab already in that room. **No stones** means nothing matched the search; **No slabs** means that stone has no free bundles.

---

### Adding a room

1. At the bottom of the **Rooms** card, type in **New room name**.
2. Click **Add Room**. An empty room appears with **No slabs in this room**. You can rename it in its header or remove it with **×**.
3. Click **Add Slab**, pick the new room, and add a slab to it.

A new room is saved only once a slab is added to it. Closing the dialog discards empty rooms.

---

### Editing a room's square feet

1. Next to **Total sqft per room:**, click the **pencil**.
2. Type the square feet (leave blank to clear it).
3. Click **Save** or press **Enter**. Click **×** to cancel.

The list's **Sqft** column adds up each room's square feet. Empty rooms show **-** and cannot be edited.

#### Closing

Click **Close** (or click outside the dialog) to return to the list with your filters unchanged.

---

### Typical shop workflow

1. Keep **Status** on **In Progress**; optionally pick a **Sales Rep**.
2. Find the job in the table, or search by customer, bundle, or stone.
3. Open it and work room by room.
4. When a slab is fully used, choose **Cut**. When a usable remnant is left, choose **Partial** and enter the leftover size.
5. If you must use a different bundle of the same stone before cutting, choose **Replace**.
6. If the job needs another slab, choose **Add Slab** (add a room first if needed).
7. Click **Close** and move on to the next job.

When every slab is cut, the status shows **Cut**. Installation is recorded by office staff in the Employee sidebar **Transactions** (**⋯** → **Mark as Installed**), which becomes available once every slab is cut. Cutting does not send emails or notifications.

---

### Shop vs Employee vs Admin transactions

The same sales also appear on **Transactions** in the Employee and Admin sidebars. Differences in short: only the shop portal and the Admin editor have **Partial**, **Replace**, **Remove**, **Add Slab**, **Add Room** and room square feet; the Employee page has simple **Cut** / **Uncut** plus **Mark as Installed** and **Contract** in each row's **⋯** menu; no transactions page sells new slabs (that's **Inventory > Stones**). Full details: **Transactions — Employee & Admin**.

---

### Other shop sidebar pages

- **Samples** — sample counts for your company's displayed stones: **Image**, **Name**, **Amount** (type a number and press **Enter**, click the check mark, or click away to save), a **−** button to take one off, and **Importance** (**High**, **Medium**, **Low**, **Hadn't cut**). Use the stone search to find a stone, and the **Out of stock** button to change the sort order. Details: **Samples & Special Order calculator**.
- **Maintenance** — equipment and service checks for the shop (statuses **OK**, **Check today**, **Overdue**; **Mark completed**, **Completion history**, **Update hours** / **Update miles**). Only a **Shop Manager** can use **Edit mode** to **Add equipment** or add checks. Details: **Shop Maintenance**.
- **My Account** — your **Name**, **Phone**, **Email**, and **Password** (**Save Changes**), plus the **Telegram** connection. See **My Account & Telegram**.

---

### Common questions / troubleshooting

- **Why can't I open Customers, Deals, or other CRM pages?** The **Shop Worker** position locks you into the shop portal. An admin with the **Manager** position can change positions in **Admin > Company settings > Users**.
- **Why don't I see the shop sidebar?** You need the **Shop Worker** or **Shop Manager** position.
- **A job is missing from the list.** **Status** defaults to **In Progress**, which hides installed and cancelled sales; choose **All Statuses**. Also check **Sales Rep** is **All**. Search only looks inside the current filters.
- **Where is Mark as Installed?** Not in the shop portal. Office staff use **⋯** → **Mark as Installed** on Employee **Transactions** after every slab is cut.
- **Replace says "Uncut slab before replace".** The slab is cut. Choose **Uncut** first, then **Replace**.
- **Replace shows "No available slabs".** Every other bundle of that stone is sold. Use **Add Slab** for a different stone, then **Remove** the old slab.
- **Remove says "Cannot remove last slab".** A sale must keep at least one slab. To cancel the whole sale, a sales rep uses **Unsell** on the sale from **Inventory > Stones**.
- **My new room disappeared.** Rooms are saved only when a slab is added to them.
- **Clicking Done in Partial does nothing.** Both **Length** and **Width** must be greater than zero.
- **The remnant disappeared after I marked Cut.** **Cut** removes the slab's unsold leftover pieces. Use **Partial** when a usable piece remains.
- **Can I change the customer, prices, sinks, or sell a slab here?** No. Those are done from the sale in **Inventory > Stones** by a sales rep.
- **A "sample" sale appeared during the guided tour.** It is a demo for the tour; changes to it are not saved.

## Statistics, Reports & Analytics (Admin)

Three admin pages show company numbers:

| **Statistics** (`/admin/statistics`) | Admin view → **CRM > Statistic** | Sales pipeline, customers, conversion, ratings, top colors, emails/SMS, QuickBooks sales by class — as a board of widgets |
