**Who can see them:** users with **Admin** access (switch to **Admin** in the sidebar header). Employees, shop workers and other positions do not have these pages. Employees see their own numbers on the Employee **Dashboard** instead. Shop cutting totals are on the shop **Shop Statistic** page (see **Shop portal**).

---

### Statistics page

Page title **Statistics**. The top bar (it stays visible while you scroll) has the filters and the **Edit** button.

#### Filters

- **Sales Rep** dropdown — **All** or one sales rep. Applies at once.
- **Current month** — sets the 1st of this month to today and applies it.
- **Select start date** / **Select end date** — pick dates, then click **Apply**.
- **Clear** — removes the dates and the sales rep (all time, everyone).

With no dates set, widgets count **all time**. Filters stay in the page address. While numbers reload you see **Updating statistics…**.

**Which date counts** (important when numbers don't match the deal board):

- **Deals by Sales Rep** and **Deals by Stage** — deals whose **last update** falls in the range.
- **Conversion Metrics** and the **Customers** table's deals — deals **created** in the range.
- Customer counts — **leads** by the day they were **assigned**, other customers by the day they were **created**.
- **Top Sold Colors** — sale date. **Sales Rep Ratings** — survey date. **Emails/SMS per Month** — send date.

#### The widgets

| Widget | What it shows |
|--------|---------------|
| **Deals by Sales Rep** | Chart of **Sales** (won) vs **Lost** per rep, and a table: **Sales Rep**, **Average Amount**, **Sales**, **Average Amount Won**, **Won %** (won ÷ won+lost), **Walk-in Won %**, **Leads Won %** |
| **Deals by Stage** | Open (not won/lost) deals per deal-board stage: **Stage**, **Deals** (count and % of all open deals), **Total Amount** |
| **Sales Rep Ratings** | Average post-install survey rating (1–5) per rep: **Sales Rep**, **Avg Rating**, **Responses** |
| **Top Campaigns** (*Top Campaigns by Customers Acquired*) | Up to 8 marketing campaigns: **Campaign Name**, **Customers Acquired**, **Conversion %** (*Conversion = Won Deals ÷ Closed Deals per Campaign*) |
| **Customers by Source** | Donut + table of valid customers by **Source** (**Walk-in**, **Call-in**, **Leads**, **Other**) |
| **Customers by Sales Rep** | Per rep: **Walk-in**, **Call-in**, **Leads**, **Manual added**, **Total** (invalid leads excluded) |
| **Conversion Metrics** (*by Deal Creation Date*) | Close rate per rep: **Sold (Total)**, **Closed Leads**, **Walk-in**, **Call-in** — percent of deals created that were won (leads/walk-in/call-in: won in the same month) |
| **Customers** | Full customer list for the filters (see below) |
| **Top Sold Colors** (*Most Popular Sold Colors*) | Top 10 stones by whole slabs sold on non-cancelled sales: **Color**, **Slabs**, **Sq ft** |
| **Emails per Month** | Outbound CRM emails sent by your team per month (**Month**, **Sent**) |
| **SMS per Month** | Outbound SMS sent from Granite Manager per month. Shows *SMS is not enabled for this company.* without CloudTalk/RingCentral |
| **Sales by Class** (QuickBooks) | QuickBooks "Sales by Class" totals (accrual) for the date range: **Class**, **Total**, chart of the top 12 classes. Only when QuickBooks is turned on for the company; messages *QuickBooks is not connected for this company.*, *Could not load QuickBooks sales by class.*, *No class sales for this period.* |

Most widgets show a chart and a table; empty periods show a short "No … for this period." message.

#### The Customers widget

Columns (sortable): **Date**, **Source**, **Sales Rep**, **Reference** (how they heard of you), **Form** (lead form), **Name**, **Status** (**Won**, **Lost**, **Invalid**, or the deal's stage), **Lost reason** (or the invalid reason), **Amount**, and a **⋯** menu. Paginated (50 per page by default, page size adjustable).

**Find customer or company** (search box in the widget header) finds a customer, jumps to the right page of the table and highlights the row for 2 seconds. Each result also has a **ban** icon (**Invalid**).

#### Marking a lead invalid

Use this for junk leads (wrong number, out of area, etc.) so they stop counting as real customers.

1. In the **Customers** widget, click **⋯** → **Invalid** on the row (or the ban icon in **Find customer or company** results).
2. Dialog **Mark invalid: [name]** → **Reason**: **Out of area**, **Wrong number, email, etc.**, **Accident submission**, **Looking for unrelated service**, or **Other** (type your own in **Enter custom value**).
3. Click **Save** (or **Cancel**). Toast: **Customer marked invalid**.

What happens: the reason is saved on the customer, their **sales rep is removed**, and **all their deals are deleted** (recorded in the customer's history). Invalid customers drop out of the source/rep counts and show **Invalid** in the table. Only admins and Sales Managers can mark leads invalid. There is no "make valid again" button on this page.

#### Customizing the board (Edit mode)

1. Click **Edit** (pencil). The bar shows **Done** and **Add widget**; each widget becomes a tile.
2. **Reorder** — drag a tile by its handle (**Drag to reorder**).
3. **Chart / Table** chips — hide or show the chart or the table of that widget (one of them always stays on).
4. **×** on a tile removes the widget.
5. **Add widget** — pick one or more in the dialog (grouped **QuickBooks**, **Deals**, **Customers**, **Performance**, **Communication**), then **Add widget** / **Add N widgets**. Each shows a short description: QuickBooks Sales by Class *Sales totals by class from the connected QuickBooks company*; Deals by Sales Rep *Won and lost deals by sales rep*; Deals by Stage *Open pipeline by deal stage*; Sales Rep Ratings *Average customer ratings by sales rep*; Top Campaigns by Customers Acquired *Customers acquired and conversion by campaign*; Customers by Source *Walk-in, call-in, leads, and other sources*; Customers by Sales Rep *Customers assigned to each sales rep*; **Conversion Metrics (by Deal Creation Date)** *Close rates by sales rep and source*; Customers *Customer list for the selected filters*; Most Popular Sold Colors *Best-selling stone colors from completed slab sales*; Sent Emails per Month *Outbound CRM emails sent by your team each month*; Sent SMS per Month *Outbound SMS sent from Granite Manager each month*. *All widgets are already on this page.* when none are left.
6. Click **Done**.

The layout is saved in **this browser** for your company (another computer or browser keeps its own layout). An empty board says *No widgets on this page. Turn on Edit to add widgets.* New companies may start with an empty board.

## Superuser Dashboard — Analytics (AI Dashboard, Widget analytics, Onboarding analytics)

Three reports in the **Superuser Dashboard** sidebar section: **AI Dashboard** (what the AI features cost and how often they run), **Widget analytics** (how people use Employee **Dashboard** widgets) and **Onboarding analytics** (how far a company's team got through the guided tours). All three are read only.

**Who can see them:** platform superusers only (Granite Manager staff). Regular admins, **Manager**s and **Super Admin**s don't have the **Superuser Dashboard** section. **Onboarding analytics** additionally shows in the sidebar only while your current company's **Onboarding** feature is on.

**Where to find them:** switch to the **Admin** side → sidebar **Superuser Dashboard** → **AI Dashboard**, **Widget analytics** or **Onboarding analytics**.

---

### AI Dashboard (`/admin/superuser-dashboard/analytics`)

Shows AI usage across all companies (or one company): spend in US dollars, number of requests, success rate, per AI feature.

#### Filters (top of the page)

- **Date range** button — presets **7d**, **30d**, **90d**, **This month**, **All time**, or pick a custom range in the two-month calendar and click **Apply**. Default: the last 30 days.
- **All time** button — from the first recorded call to today.
- **Company** dropdown — **All companies** or one company (shown when there is more than one company).

The range, company and page are kept in the address, so a copied link opens the same view.

A yellow warning **Unpriced model(s) in this range — cost is logging as $0** can appear when an AI model has no price set; those calls count as requests but show $0. It is for Granite Manager developers; the **X** hides it.

#### Summary cards

- **Spend this month** — month-to-date spend, the change vs last month, and **All time** spend.
- **Spend in range** — spend between the selected dates.
- **Requests in range** — number of AI calls, with the average cost per request.
- **Success rate** — share of AI calls in the range that succeeded.

#### Chart

Title changes with the tab: **Spend by feature**, **Usage by feature** or **Cost per request**.
- Tabs **Spend**, **Requests**, **Avg $/req** pick the measure.
- **Bars** / **Donut** pick the chart. **Donut** is not available for **Avg $/req**.
- Each feature keeps its own color. Hover a legend entry to highlight that feature; hover a bar or slice for its value.

#### Features table

*Click a feature for details.* Columns: **Feature**, **Works with** (input → output, e.g. text, image, audio), **Models**, **Requests**, **Cost** (click **Requests** or **Cost** to sort; click again to reverse), **Share of spend** (bar), **Success** (green check at 98% or more, red warning below). A feature the dashboard doesn't recognize is marked **Unregistered**.

Tracked features include **AI Chat Assistant**, **Email Generation**, **Automated Follow-Ups**, **Quick Reply Suggestions**, **AI Image Creation**, **Call Transcription**, **Call Activity Extraction**, **Call Note Summarization**, **Email Improvement**, **Supplier Price List OCR**, **Customer Activity AI Search**, **CRM Manual Corrections**, **Teach Mode Quiz Generation**, **Email Template Generation**, **QuickBooks Invoice AI Edit**, **Call Coaching**, **Call Points Classification** and **Signature Field Detection**.

#### Feature details

Click a feature row (or a row in **Last actions**) to open its dialog: a description, **Works with**, **Used in** (links to the pages that use it), **Models**, then for the selected range **Requests**, **Total cost**, **Avg cost/call**, **Success rate**, **Avg input tokens**, **Avg output tokens**, a **Top users** table (**User**, **Requests**, **Cost**) and **Recent calls** (**When**, **User**, **Model**, **Tokens in/out**, **Cost**, **OK**). **Show more** loads 20 more calls.

#### Last actions

*Most recent AI calls in this range, 20 per page by default.* Columns: **When**, **Feature**, **User**, **Company**, **Model**, **Tokens in/out**, **Cost**, **Duration**, **OK** (check = success, warning = failed). Change page or page size below the table. Calls made by automatic jobs (not a person) show **Background job** as the user.

Empty states: *No AI usage recorded in this range yet. Data appears within minutes of using any AI feature.* / *No AI calls recorded in this range yet.*

---

### Widget analytics (`/admin/superuser-dashboard/widget-analytics`)

*How people use employee dashboard widgets, by company and user.* Covers all companies.

- **Summary cards** — **Events** (every tracked widget interaction), **Users** (people who used a widget), **Companies** (companies with widget activity), **Top interaction** (the most-used widget action and its count).
- **Top used** — interactions (clicks and goal changes) ranked across all companies.
- **Top added widgets** — widgets currently on dashboards, ranked by how many dashboards have them.
- **Currently added widgets** — *Widgets each user has on their dashboard right now* (**Company**, **User**, **Widget**), 25 per page. A user appears after they open their dashboard.
- **By company and user** — *Who used or added each widget*: a **Uses** table (**#**, **Company**, **User**, **Interaction**, **Uses**) and an **Adds** table (**#**, **Company**, **User**, **Widget**, **Times added**).
- **All events** — *Every click, goal change, add, and remove, newest first* (**When**, **Company**, **User**, **Widget**, **Action**: click, change, add or remove), 25 per page.

Empty states: *No widget interactions yet.*, *No saved dashboard widgets yet.*, *No widget events yet.*

---

### Onboarding analytics (`/admin/onboarding-analytics`)

Page heading **Onboarding analytics** — *Every guided tour your team can see, how many of them get finished, and the exact step people walk away on.* It covers the employees of your **current company** only.

**When it is available:** the sidebar item shows only while the company's **Onboarding** feature is on (switch on the company's card in **Superuser Dashboard > Companies**). If the feature is off, opening the page sends you back to Admin.

#### End state vs. live funnel

A note explains the page shows where the team stands **right now** (completion, skips, last step seen) — not how long an unfinished tour has been sitting or where people give up inside a tour before closing it. Those live-funnel questions are answered in PostHog; **Open PostHog** opens it in a new tab.

#### Summary

- A large percentage — *of the N tours your M people can see have been finished.*
- *x of M have finished every tour open to them*; *N tours were met and then left unfinished*; *N people have not met a single tour yet*.
- A bar split into **Finished** (reached the reward card and earned the points), **In progress**, **Skipped**, **Not started**, with a legend.
- An activity strip of tours finished and skipped over the last weeks (hover a week for its numbers).

#### Tour by tour

*Open a row to see the step people walk away on.* Sort by **Lowest finish rate** or **Most people**; **Search tours**. Each row shows the tour name, an outcome bar, finished / people (e.g. *4/9*), the finish rate and the step most people left at (e.g. *2 left at …*). Click a row to expand it: a summary, the steps with how many people reached each, the people and their state on that tour, the number of steps, and counts such as *… said yes but have not reached a step yet* or *… closed the announcement without opening it*. *Visible to no one* means no one on the team gets that tour.

#### Person by person

*Least finished first. Open a row for the detail.*
- Filters: **Everyone**, **Still has tours left**, **Skipped something**, **Never opened one** (each with a count).
- **Search people**.
- **Copy emails** — copies the email addresses of the people shown (*Copied* / *Copy failed*).
- **Download CSV** — downloads the people shown as *onboarding-progress-YYYY-MM-DD.csv* with **Name**, **Email**, **Tours available**, **Finished**, **Skipped**, **In progress**, **Not started**, **Points**, **Last active**.
- Sortable columns **Person**, **Finished**, **Skipped**, **Points**, **Last active**.
- Opening a person lists every tour with its state, e.g. *Finished on …*, *Closed the announcement without opening the tour*, *Left on step 3, "…"*, *Paused on step 2, "…"*, *Opened, but no step reached yet*, *Has not met this tour yet*.

When the company has no employees yet: *No employees yet* — the report fills in as people meet the guided tours.

### Common questions

- **I can't find AI Dashboard / Widget analytics.** They are in **Superuser Dashboard**, on the Admin side, for platform superusers only.
- **Onboarding analytics is missing from the sidebar.** Turn on **Onboarding** for your company on its card in **Superuser Dashboard > Companies**.

## Superuser Dashboard — Companies

The **Companies** page is where Granite Manager platform superusers manage every company on the platform: create a company, edit its details and integration keys, turn features on or off, check its setup progress, view its users, and delete it.

**Who can see it:** platform superusers only (Granite Manager staff accounts). Regular admins, **Manager**s and **Super Admin**s do not have this page and cannot be given it from **Users** — the superuser flag is set by Granite Manager. Shop staff who need a company change should ask Granite Manager support.

**Where to find it:** switch to the **Admin** side (header **Admin** / **Employee** button) → sidebar **Superuser Dashboard** (collapsible section) → **Companies**. The section is only in the Admin sidebar. Opening **Superuser Dashboard** without picking an item also lands on **Companies**. The page heading reads **Superuser Dashboard**.

### The companies list (`/admin/superuser-dashboard/companies`)

At the top: the **Create Company** and **Texting registrations (10DLC)** buttons and a count such as *12 companies*. Companies are listed as cards, companies with the most users first. Each card shows:

- **Logo and name** — the logo, or the company's initials when there is none. Click the name or logo to open the **company info** dialog.
- **… (Actions) menu** — top-right of the card: **Edit**, **Telnyx** (Granite Phone setup), **10DLC texting** (the company's texting registration: its Telnyx statuses, **Send to Telnyx**, **Refresh**, **Send again** after a rejection, the company's **Numbers** to assign once approved, the form to review or edit with **Save changes**, and **Ask AI**, the chat beside the form that sees it and the company) and **Delete**. **Send to Telnyx** and **Send again** work only when the AI check passed this form within the last 24 hours (pages change): an older check, or none, runs again first and the send says *The AI check is more than a day old (or never ran), so it runs again now: send it once it passes, in a few minutes*; superusers are told in the bell when it passes, and when it finds changes the registration goes back to **Draft** and the company is emailed them.
- **Inbox score** — the email-deliverability rating of the company's domain (its button: *View deliverability recommendations* or *View deliverability status*): **🟢 Good**, **🟡 Review**, **🔴 High Risk** or **⚪ Unknown**, with a score. Click it to open the **Email deliverability** dialog (status, or actions that would improve the score for that domain). *No inbox score* means no domain is set or the check has not run.
  - **What the score means:** an estimate of the spam / inbox risk of email from the domain, read from its DNS (lower is better): **0–20 Good**, **21–50 Review**, **51–100 High Risk**. The dialog shows **Checked domain:**, the score, and **Findings** (green: OK, amber: a problem), for example *MX ok*, *SPF ok* or *SPF missing*, *DMARC p=none*, *DKIM found*, or the domain *listed on* a spam blocklist (Spamhaus).
  - **How to improve this score** — the fixes, *ordered by certainty: known problems first*. Each is marked **Certain fix** (a definite DNS problem; fixing it improves the score) or **Likely helps**, and shows the **Current record** and the **Recommended record** (or **Suggested record** when there is none) to put in the domain's DNS. Examples: **Publish SPF record** / **Update SPF record**, **Fix dangerous SPF +all**, **Add or update DMARC**, **Fix conflicting DMARC records**, **Strengthen DMARC policy** (from *p=none* to quarantine or reject), **Enable Google Workspace DKIM** / **Enable Microsoft 365 DKIM**, **Add MX records**, getting off a blocklist. When nothing would help: *No DNS changes needed to improve this score for <domain>.*
  - The DNS changes are made where the company's domain is hosted (its registrar or DNS provider), not in Granite Manager. The domain is checked again when the company is saved.
- **SES badge** — inbound email status of the domain: **SES connected**, **SES pending** or **SES off**, plus **Inbound on** (the domain receives mail into the CRM) or **MX inbound**. Hover for the details.
- **Setup** tile — checklist items done / total, e.g. *9/14*. Click it to open the **Setup checklist**.
- **Users** tile — active users / **Max Users** (— when there is no limit). Turns amber when the company is over its limit. Walk-in accounts do not count.
- **Onboarding** tile — users who finished the first guided tour / users who take tours (installer and walk-in accounts don't take tours).
- **Features** switches — **QuickBooks**, **eSignatures**, **Onboarding**, **Leaderboard** (see below). Each saves the moment you flip it.
- **Billing** switch — **Require Stripe payment**.
- **CloudTalk** and **QuickBooks** chips at the bottom — filled when connected (CloudTalk keys saved; a QuickBooks company linked).

If the list fails to load: *Could not load companies. Refresh the page and try again.*

#### Feature switches on the card

| Switch | What it turns on for that company |
|--------|-----------------------------------|
| **QuickBooks** | Invoices, QuickBooks connect, and sales widgets. On by default. |
| **eSignatures** | Sending documents for signature. Each user also needs their own access in **Superuser Dashboard > Feature Access**. |
| **Onboarding** | The guided tours, and the **Onboarding analytics** report for that company. When never set, the platform default applies. |
| **Leaderboard** | The points leaderboard on the Employee **Dashboard**. When never set, the platform default applies. |

If a switch can't be saved, a toast **Error** says *Could not save the switch* (or the reason) and the switch goes back.

#### Require Stripe payment

- **On** — *Access depends on the Stripe subscription*: the company must keep a paid Stripe subscription (**Billing**) to use the app.
- **Off** — *Works without Stripe (ACH, cash, manual)*: for companies that pay some other way.

### Creating a company

1. **Superuser Dashboard > Companies** → **Create Company**.
2. Fill in the **Create Company** dialog:
   - **Company Name** — required.
   - **Subdomain** — required; lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens only (e.g. *acmestone* gives *acmestone.granite-manager.com*). Must be unique.
   - **Company address** — optional, with address suggestions.
   - **Sales Tax (%)** — optional, 0 to 100 (e.g. 7).
   - **Domain / company email** — optional: the company's email domain or an address at it (e.g. *acmestone.com* or *owner@acmestone.com*). Used for the inbox score, inbound email (SES) and the setup checklist.
   - **CloudTalk Access Key** and **CloudTalk Access Secret** — optional (see below).
   - **RingCentral Client ID**, **RingCentral Client Secret**, **RingCentral JWT**, **RingCentral Server URL** — optional (see below).
3. Click **Create**. Toast: **Company created**, and the dialog closes.

**What creating a company sets up automatically:** the system calendars, the default company email templates, the customer sources **Walk-in**, **Leads**, **Call-in** and **Other**, the **Statistic** page widgets starting hidden, a **Walk-in** employee account named *walk-in@<subdomain>.com* for the check-in kiosk, and a first deliverability check of the domain.

**What it does not do:** it does **not** create an admin or any staff user. Add the company's people afterwards in **Admin > Company settings > Users** → **Add User** (a superuser picks the company there). Logo, **Max Users** and the feature switches are set afterwards with **Edit**.

Errors: *Company name is required*; *Subdomain is required*; *Subdomain must contain only lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens*; *Sales tax must be between 0 and 100*; *Subdomain is already in use* (shown under **Subdomain**); otherwise *Could not create the company* at the top of the dialog.

### Editing a company

1. On the company's card open the **…** menu → **Edit** (or open the company info dialog → **Edit company**).
2. The **Edit Company — <name>** dialog shows **CloudTalk Connected / Not connected** and **QuickBooks Connected / Not connected** badges and these sections:
   - **Company details** — **Company name**, **Subdomain**, **Domain / company email**, **Company address**.
   - **Branding** — **Logo** (upload an image) and a **Logo height** control (32–192 px) for how tall the logo shows in the app header.
   - **Limits** — **Sales Tax (%)** (0–100) and **Max Users** (blank = *Unlimited*; whole number, 1 or more).
   - **Features** — **QuickBooks** (*Invoices, QuickBooks connect, and sales widgets*) and **eSignatures** (*Requires individual user access*).
   - **Integrations** — **CloudTalk Access Key**, **CloudTalk Access Secret**, **RingCentral Client ID**, **RingCentral Client Secret**, **RingCentral JWT**, **RingCentral Server URL**. The current values are filled in.
3. Click **Save**. Toast: **Company updated**. The domain's deliverability is re-checked.

Notes:
- Clearing a key field and saving removes that key (CloudTalk or RingCentral then shows as not connected).
- **Max Users** is a soft limit: when a company is at or over it, **Add User** shows a notice but still lets you add the user. Walk-in accounts don't count.
- **QuickBooks** is not connected here. The company connects it in **Admin > Company settings > Company** (**Connect QuickBooks**). **RingCentral** can also be connected there with **Connect RingCentral** instead of typing keys.
- **Onboarding** and **Leaderboard** are not in this dialog — use the switches on the company card.
- Errors: *Subdomain is already in use*, or a toast **Error** — *Could not save the company*.

#### Where to get the CloudTalk Access Key and Access Secret

You get them from CloudTalk, then paste them into Granite Manager:

1. Log in to the CloudTalk Dashboard (dashboard.cloudtalk.io) with **CloudTalk Admin** access.
2. Go to **Account → Settings → API Keys**.
3. Click **+ Add API Key** (or use an existing key).
4. Copy the **Access Key ID** and **Access Key Secret** (use **Show** to reveal the secret).
5. In Granite Manager: **Superuser Dashboard > Companies** → **Create Company**, or the company's **…** → **Edit**.
6. Paste them into **CloudTalk Access Key** and **CloudTalk Access Secret**, then **Create** / **Save**.

CloudTalk counts as connected only when both are saved. Each sales rep still needs their **CloudTalk agent ID** and **CloudTalk phone number** on their user (**Admin > Company settings > Users** → **Edit**, or **My Account**) before SMS and call history work for them.

#### RingCentral fields

**RingCentral Client ID**, **Client Secret** and **JWT** come from the company's RingCentral developer app and its JWT credential; **RingCentral Server URL** is normally *https://platform.ringcentral.com* (the field's example). RingCentral counts as connected on the setup checklist when Client ID, Client Secret and JWT are all saved.

#### Telnyx

Telnyx (Granite Phone) is not on **Create Company** or **Edit Company**: it has its own dialog. On the company's card open **…** → **Telnyx** (**Telnyx — <company>**): **Calling enabled**, the Telnyx portal ids (**Credential connection ID**, **TeXML application ID**, **Outbound voice profile ID**, **Billing group ID**, **Telnyx account ID**, **AI Assistant ID**, **Messaging profile ID**, **Fallback TeXML URL**), **Recording**, **Business hours and holidays**, then **Save** and paste the **Webhooks** URLs it shows into the Telnyx portal. The company's admins then import and assign the numbers on **Admin > Company settings > Phone**. See **Granite Phone (Telnyx)** for every field and the Phone page.

The **Superuser Dashboard** is a sidebar section for Granite Manager platform superusers (Granite Manager staff). It holds the tools that work across every company on the platform: companies, feature access, AI costs, chat-answer corrections, analytics, user feedback, bug reports and the sales mailbox.

**Who can see it:** platform superusers only. It is not tied to a position: regular admins, **Manager**s and users with the **Super Admin** position do not see it, and the superuser flag cannot be turned on from **Users** — Granite Manager sets it. Other users who open one of these pages by link get no data.

**Where to find it:** switch to the **Admin** side (header **Admin** / **Employee** button) → sidebar **Superuser Dashboard** (click the section name to expand it). The section is only in the **Admin** sidebar, never the Employee one. Every page in it shows the heading **Superuser Dashboard** (except **Onboarding analytics**, which has its own heading).

### Feature Access (`/admin/superuser-dashboard/feature-access`)

- **Search** — *Search by name, email, or company*.

What users see without access: trying to send a document for signature opens **Signatures access required** — *Ask your manager for access to signatures before you can send a document for signing.* If the company's eSignatures feature is off, the send fails saying eSignatures are turned off for this company and a superuser can turn them on in **Companies** → **Edit** → **eSignatures**.

### Instruction corrections (`/admin/superuser-dashboard/instruction-corrections`)

**Superuser Dashboard > Instruction corrections** collects chat (CRM manual) answers that users disliked, so the manual can be fixed.

**How items get here:** in the sidebar **Chat**, a user clicks **Not helpful** on a manual answer and gets a corrected answer (up to two tries). Then:
- **Helpful** on a corrected answer → saved as **User approved correction** (*Thanks — your review was saved for our team.*).
- **Still not helpful** on the first correction → the chat tries a second correction.
- **Still not helpful** on the second correction → saved as **Escalated review** (*I'm sorry — your review was added to our team and we will check it.*).

**Each card shows:** the type (**User approved correction** or **Escalated review**), company · user · date, the conversation as chat bubbles (question, **Original answer**, **Correction 1/2** marked *liked* or *disliked*), and — when the chat suggested one — a **Manual update** note with the **Section** and **Proposed change**.

**Buttons:**
- **Approve manual update** — writes the proposed text into that manual section, so the chat uses it from then on, and closes the item. Disabled when there is no proposed change or section.
- **Mark reviewed** — closes the item without changing the manual.

Either way the card leaves the list. Empty: *No pending instruction corrections.*

## Teach Mode & Employee Progress (Training Quizzes)

**Teach Mode** turns your company's instructions (**Resources > Instructions**) into multiple-choice quizzes. Admins generate questions with AI or write them by hand; employees take the test for an instruction and must get every answer right to mark it completed; admins then check each sales rep's answers on **Employee Progress**.

---

### How to get there (no sidebar item)

Teach Mode currently has **no sidebar item** on either side, and Employee Progress has none either. Ways in:

| Page | How to open it |
|------|----------------|
| **Teach Mode** (employee test) | Open the address `/employee/teach-mode`; or, on the Admin Teach Mode page, click the header **Employee** button (it opens Employee Teach Mode); or the **Teach Mode** row in **Guided walkthrough** inside the **Onboarding** widget on the Employee **Dashboard** (starts a guided tour on that page). |
| **Teach Mode** (admin: create and manage questions) | Open the address `/admin/teach-mode`; or click the header **Admin** button while on Employee Teach Mode; or the **Teach Mode** row under **Admin** in **Guided walkthrough**. |
| **Employee Progress** | On Admin **Teach Mode**, click **Employee progress** (top right). An answer to a question that was deleted or changed may show *Question text missing* or *Correct answer missing*. |

Note: the guided-tour text that says *Teach Mode is under Resources* is out of date — there is no Teach Mode item under **Resources**.

### Who can use it

| Who | What they can do |
|-----|------------------|
| Any employee (Employee side) | Take tests on **Teach Mode** |
| Users with **Admin** access (and platform superusers) | Generate, add, edit, delete, publish and hide questions on Admin **Teach Mode**; open **Employee Progress** |

Teach Mode is **not** filtered by an instruction's **Visible to** positions: every published question is offered to every employee, whatever their position. There is no way to limit a quiz to certain positions.

---

### Admin: Teach Mode (`/admin/teach-mode`)

Heading **Teach Mode** — *Generate complete assessments from instructions, then review and publish them.*

#### Generate questions with AI

1. In the **Generate questions** card, choose an **Instruction**. The list shows all of your company's instructions as a tree (sub-instructions indented with —). The onboarding sample instructions and the AI follow-up instruction are not offered.
2. Click **Generate Questions**. The button shows a spinner; it can take a minute or two.
3. The AI reads the instruction's text and writes multiple-choice questions with **four answers** each, enough to cover all of its meaningful information — at most **30** per click. It is told the instruction's existing questions and tries not to repeat them.
4. Toast **Success** — *N questions generated and visible to employees*. New questions are **published right away**.

Clicking **Generate Questions** again **adds** more questions; it never replaces existing ones.

Errors (toast **Error**): *This instruction has no content to generate questions from* (the instruction has no text — add content in **Resources > Instructions** first); *The AI returned invalid question data* / *The AI did not generate usable questions* (try again). If the company has no instructions: *Add an instruction before generating questions.*

#### Reviewing the questions

Under **Questions** (*N for this instruction. New questions are visible to employees by default.*) each question is a card with the instruction name, the question, its answers (the correct one highlighted green) and a switch at the bottom. Only the selected instruction's questions are listed. Empty: *No questions for this instruction yet. Generate the first assessment.*

#### Add a question manually

1. Choose the instruction, then click **Add question manually** (the button changes to **Cancel**).
2. In **Add a question**: type the **Question**, fill the **Answers** boxes (four are shown) and select the radio button next to the correct one (the first is selected to start).
3. Click **Save question**. Toast: **Question added**.

Rules: the question text is required (*Enter the question text*); empty answer boxes are ignored; at least two answers are needed (*At least two answers are required*); exactly one must be correct (*Choose exactly one correct answer*). Manually added questions are visible to employees right away.

#### Edit a question

1. Click **Edit** on the card.
2. Change the **Question** text; change answers, pick the correct one with the radio button, **Remove** answers or **Add answer**.
3. Click **Save changes** (toast **Question updated**) or **Cancel**.

Editing does not change answers employees already submitted.

#### Delete a question

Click **Delete** → dialog **Delete question** — *Delete this question? Employees stop seeing it.* → **Delete**. Toast: **Question deleted**. Answers already given to it stay in **Employee Progress**.

#### Publish or hide (drafts)

- The switch on each card shows **Visible to employees** (on) or **Draft — hidden from employees** (off). Flipping it saves at once: toast **Question published** or **Question moved to drafts**.
- When the selected instruction has hidden questions, **Make all visible (N)** publishes all of them: toast *N questions made visible to employees* (or *All questions for this instruction are already visible*).

---

### Employee: Teach Mode (`/employee/teach-mode`)

*Choose an instruction, answer every question, then click Submit Test. Passing marks that instruction as completed.*

#### Taking a test

1. Pick an instruction in the **Instruction** dropdown. Only instructions with at least one published question appear, sorted by title; ones you passed show **(Completed)**. The page opens on the first instruction you haven't completed.
2. Answer each question by clicking an answer. Questions and answers come in a random order each time.
3. Click **Submit Test**. If some are unanswered, a prompt says *You have N unanswered questions. Click OK to submit anyway, or Cancel to return to the test.* Unanswered questions count as wrong.

#### Results

- **Your Score: N%** appears at the top. Each question shows **✓ Correct** next to the right answer, a wrong pick in red, and *✅ Correct!* or *❌ Incorrect. The correct answer is: …*.
- **100%** — *Test finished. Review your answers below, or retake anytime.* Toast **Test finished** — *Test finished with 100%. This instruction is marked completed.* The instruction now shows **(Completed)**.
- **Below 100%** — *Review your mistakes below. Click Retake Test when you are ready to try again. You need 100% to finish.* Toast **Not finished** — *Your score is N%. You need 100% to finish this test.*
- **Retake Test** starts again with a fresh shuffle. You can retake a passed test too.

Every submission is saved (including retakes and failed tries) and shows on **Employee Progress**. If saving fails: toast **Error** — *Failed to save attempts: …*.

#### Empty states

- *No Questions Available — There is nothing to take yet. Ask an administrator to generate questions in Teach Mode and turn on Visible to employees for each question.*
- *No Questions For This Instruction — Choose another instruction from the list above.*

During the onboarding guided tour a **sample test** appears first in the list; it is only for practice and is not saved.

#### When an instruction counts as completed

An instruction is **Completed** for you when, in one submission, you answered **all** of its currently published questions correctly. So if an admin later publishes a new question for that instruction, **(Completed)** disappears until you pass the test again. Hiding or deleting a question doesn't take away a completion.

---

### Admin: Employee Progress (`/admin/employee-progress`)

Heading **Employee Progress** — *Welcome, <your email>! Select a user and click the button below.* **Back to Teach Mode** returns to Admin Teach Mode.

1. In **Select Employee:** choose a person (*name (email)*). The list contains only users with the **Sales Representative** position in your company.
2. Click **Check User Progress** (disabled until someone is chosen).
3. **Progress for: <name>** lists every attempt, newest first, as collapsed rows like **Attempt 2 — 7/8 (87.5%)**. Click a row to expand it.
4. The table shows **Correct** (✅ right, ❌ wrong), **Question**, **Selected Answer** (*No answer provided* when skipped) and **Correct Answer**.

Messages: *Select a user and click "Check User Progress" to view their quiz history.*; *Click "Check User Progress" to load quiz attempts.*; *No quiz attempts found for this user.*

Things to know:
- Attempts are numbered **per instruction**, and this page groups them by number only — **Attempt 1** contains the person's first try at every instruction they took, **Attempt 2** their second tries, and so on. The instruction name is not shown; the questions tell you which test it was.
- Answers to questions that were later deleted or hidden are still listed.
- The page is read only: you can't reset, delete or excuse attempts.

- **Why is Teach Mode not in my sidebar?** The sidebar item was removed. Use the address `/employee/teach-mode` (or `/admin/teach-mode` for admins), the **Admin** / **Employee** header button from the other Teach Mode page, or **Guided walkthrough** in the Dashboard **Onboarding** widget.

## Texting registration (10DLC): the carriers' form for business SMS

US carriers block business texts (SMS) sent from local phone numbers until the business and how it texts are registered. This registration is called **10DLC** (also A2P 10DLC, brand and campaign registration). In Granite Manager it is the **Texting registration (10DLC)** form, for companies that text through **Granite Phone (Telnyx)**. When someone asks how to fill out "the form for SMS", "the SMS registration" or "the texting form", this is it.

**Who fills it out:** users with the **Manager** position. Others see *Only your company's Managers fill out the texting registration.*

**Where to find it:**
- Admins: **Admin > Company settings > Phone** (`/admin/phone`) → the **Texting registration (10DLC)** card → **Fill it out** (later **Continue**, or **View** once it can no longer be edited).
- Managers who are not admins: the **Texting registration** page (`/employee/texting-registration`), which is not in the sidebar during the rollout.

The form has three steps, the buttons at its top: **1. Business**, **2. How you text** and **3. Review**. A step with a check mark is complete. **Save draft** keeps what you typed so you can finish later.

**The first draft:** the first time it opens, the form is already filled in from what Granite Manager knows: **Private company (LLC, Inc.)**, **Construction and remodeling**, the company's name as both **Business name** and **Legal name**, **United States**, the Manager's name and email, the company's main Granite Phone number, the website from the company's email domain, **Several kinds (mixed)** with **Customer care**, **Account updates** and **Marketing**, and texts, keyword answers and keywords written with the business name. Check every field: the **Tax id (EIN)** and the address are empty, and the **Legal name** must be changed when the IRS has a different one.

**AI helper (Ask AI):** the **Ask AI** button at the top of the form opens a chat beside it (*Ask about this form*) (on a phone the chat fills the window; its **X** goes back to the form). It sees the form as you fill it in, unsaved changes included, the step you are on, what is still missing, your company's details (name, address, website, phone numbers) and where the registration is (the carriers' reasons and the AI check's changes). Ask it what a field means or what to type, or ask it to write a field for you: it answers with text to paste. It knows the carriers' rules, including what your website pages must show. It can't fill in, save or send the form for you and does not open your website (the AI check does, after **Mark as ready**). Suggested questions: *What should I fix first?*, *Write my sample texts*, *What must my quote form, privacy policy and terms say?* The conversation ends when the form is closed.

---

### Step 1. Business

*Carriers check these against public records: use your exact legal details.*

**The business**
- **Type of business** — **Private company (LLC, Inc.)**, **Publicly traded company**, **Non-profit** or **Government**. Most countertop shops are a private company.
- **Industry** — usually **Construction and remodeling**.
- **Business name** — the name customers know you by. Every text names it.
- **Legal name** — exactly as the IRS has it for your EIN (your CP 575 letter).
- **Tax id (EIN)** — 9 digits, like *12-3456789*. Canadian businesses: the 9-digit business number.
- **Country of registration** — **United States** or **Canada**.

**Contact** (where carriers can reach the business)
- **Business phone** (a US or Canada number), **Business email**, **Website** (starting with *https://*; carriers visit it, so it should show your business name). Carriers look for this phone, email and the business address on your website's home page (for example in its footer): use the phone and email your website shows.
- **Contact first name** and **Contact last name** are optional.

**Business address** — as on your tax records, no PO boxes: **Street address**, **City**, **State or province** (2 letters, like *IN*), **ZIP or postal code**.

A **Publicly traded company** also enters its **Stock symbol**, **Stock exchange** and **Business contact email** (the **Public company** part).

---

### Step 2. How you text

**What you text**
- **The texts are** — the kind of texting. **Several kinds (mixed)** is the usual choice (answers, quotes, appointments and offers); **Low volume, several kinds** is for under 6,000 texts a month, with a lower fee and lower limits. The other choices, each one kind only: **Customer care** (answers and updates for customers who contacted you), **Account updates** (quotes, invoices, appointment confirmations and reminders), **Delivery updates** (order and delivery status), **Marketing** (promotions and offers), **Surveys** (surveys and polls), **Sign-in codes** (one-time codes to sign in), **Security alerts** (alerts about account security), **Fraud alerts** (alerts about possible fraud), **Public service announcements** (announcements to the public) and **Higher education** (colleges and universities). Leaving it empty says *Choose what the texts are about.* Mixed and low volume are not kinds of texts themselves: they need the kinds below.
- **Kinds of texts** — for mixed or low volume, tick the kinds you send (2 to 5 for mixed, 1 to 5 for low volume), for example **Customer care**, **Account updates** and **Marketing**.
- **What you text and why** — at least 40 characters, and it must name your business (who sends the texts). For example: *Acme Stone texts customers who asked for a quote or hired us: quotes, appointment reminders, project updates, and offers to customers who agreed.*

**How customers agree to texts**
- **How customers opt in** — at least 40 characters: where customers give you their mobile number and what they are told. It must give your quote form's address and your privacy policy's address (the same ones as under **Your website pages**). Carriers refuse vague answers. For example: *"Customers ask for a quote on our quote form at https://acmestone.com/quote and check a box, not checked in advance and not required, that says: I agree to receive texts from Acme Stone about my quote, appointments and offers. Message frequency varies. Message and data rates may apply. Reply STOP to opt out. Reply HELP for help. Privacy policy: https://acmestone.com/privacy"*. Name another way customers agree (by phone, in the showroom) only when it really happens, with the words they are told; with **Marketing**, such a way also needs a confirmation text the customer answers YES to.

**Sample texts** — 2 to 5 real examples of texts you send, at least one for each kind of texts you ticked. Each one must name your business, end with how to opt out (like *Reply STOP to opt out.*), be different from the others, and use full links (no link shorteners such as bit.ly). **Use examples** fills in ready-made samples with your business name; **Add a sample** adds another.

**Replies to keywords** — what a customer gets back after texting a keyword. Each answer names your business, and carriers require these in it:
- **Answer to HELP** — how to reach you: your phone number, email or website (*Reply STOP to opt out* is good to add). **Help keywords** must include *HELP*, for example *HELP,INFO*.
- **Answer to opting in** — what texts they will get, *Reply HELP for help*, *Msg frequency varies*, *Msg & data rates may apply* and *Reply STOP to opt out*; with **Marketing** also *Consent is not a condition of purchase*. **Opt-in keywords**, for example *START*.
- **Answer to STOP** — that they will get no more texts, like *You are unsubscribed and will receive no further messages.* **Opt-out keywords** must include *STOP*, for example *STOP,UNSUBSCRIBE,CANCEL,END,QUIT*.
- Keywords are single words of letters and digits, separated by commas.

**About the texts** — tick what is true:
- **The texts contain links** (then an optional **Example link**). Tick it exactly when a sample text has a link.
- **The texts contain phone numbers**. Tick it exactly when a sample text has a phone number.
- **We text from a pool of 50 or more numbers** (most companies do not), **age-restricted products** and **loans or direct lending**: leave unticked for a countertop shop.

**Your website pages** — required, each a full address starting with *https://*. Carriers open these pages:
- **Quote form** — the page with the form customers fill out to give their phone number and agree to texts.
- **Privacy policy**.
- **Texting terms**.

**Carrier rules** — tick *We text only people who agreed to get texts from us, stop right away when they reply STOP, and follow the carriers' rules for business texting.*

#### What your website pages must show

The carriers' reviewers open these pages, and the AI check reads them after **Mark as ready** (with the privacy and terms pages your quote form links to, when they are other pages). Most refusals come from these pages, not from the form. These are Telnyx's published requirements; missing any of them gets the registration refused.

- **Quote form** — a public page (no sign-in) with your business name or website, where customers type their phone number. A checkbox for agreeing to texts: **not checked in advance**, **not required** (customers can send the form without it), only about texts (not combined with accepting the terms, or with emails or calls), and next to the phone field. One checkbox for all your kinds of texts is fine when its words say marketing or promotional texts are included. The words by the checkbox must include: your business name; what texts customers will get (saying *marketing* or *promotional* when you send offers); *Message frequency varies*; *Message and data rates may apply*; *Reply STOP to opt out*; *Reply HELP for help*; and *We will not share mobile information with third parties for promotional or marketing purposes* (or a link to your privacy policy right there); with **Marketing** also *Consent is not a condition of purchase*. Example: *By checking this box, I agree to receive text messages from Acme Stone about customer care, account notifications and marketing offers. Message frequency varies. Message and data rates may apply. Reply STOP to opt out. Reply HELP for help. Consent is not a condition of purchase. We will not share mobile information with third parties for promotional or marketing purposes.* The page links to both your privacy policy and your terms (by the checkbox, in the footer or menu), and those must be the same pages you enter under **Your website pages**.
- **Privacy policy** — your business's own privacy policy, about what personal information you collect and how you use it (a cookie notice or a "privacy choices" page alone does not count). It must say mobile information, text opt-in data and consent are not sold **or shared** with third parties or affiliates for marketing or promotional purposes. If it says anywhere that personal information may be shared with, sold or disclosed to third parties (including a "sale" or "sharing" under state privacy laws), it must say that excludes text messaging opt-in data and consent. Wording carriers accept: *No mobile information will be shared with third parties or affiliates for marketing or promotional purposes. All the above categories exclude text messaging originator opt-in data and consent; this information will not be shared with any third parties.*
- **Texting terms** — a public page with a part on text messages that includes: your business name, what the texts are about, *Message frequency varies*, how to get help (*Reply HELP* or your phone or email), *Reply STOP to opt out* and *Message and data rates may apply*. How customers agree, carrier liability, a final confirmation after STOP and a privacy link are good to add.
- **All pages agree with the checkbox** — no page may say customers agree to texts just by giving their phone number or sending a form, or bundle texts with calls or emails; and none may say texts continue after a customer replies STOP when your answer to STOP says no more texts are sent.
- **Website** (step 1) — opens and is your working site, with a name matching the **Business name** or **Legal name**, saying clearly what the business does, and showing the **Business phone**, **Business email** and business address from step 1; not parked, for sale or under construction. It must not mention lead generation, selling leads or SEO services: carriers refuse those.

---

### Step 3. Review

Shows the business, type, tax id, address, contact, the kinds of texts and how many sample texts are written. **Still to do** lists every missing or wrong field with a **Fix it** button that opens its step. When nothing is missing: *Everything the carriers need is filled in.*

---

### Sending it

1. Click **Mark as ready** (when something is missing, the form opens **Review** with the list instead).
2. **Form submitted**: *Thank you for submitting the form. Our AI agent will check your form, and we will contact you at your email.* The check runs in the background (close the window any time) and reads the form and your quote form, privacy policy, terms and website pages, and the privacy and terms pages your quote form links to. Granite Manager first checks what it can tell for certain on the pages: that the quote form links to your privacy policy and terms and that they are the pages you entered, that its texts checkbox is there, not checked in advance and not required, and that your website shows the business phone, email and address. Then the AI checks the rest against Telnyx's published reasons for refusing registrations. It flags what carriers refuse, not wording that could merely be better. The Manager who clicked **Mark as ready** gets the result by email. When it finds problems, **Changes to make before it is sent** lists each one with **Your text** and **Replace it with** (or **Add this**). On a computer the list sits on the right of the form, and each side scrolls on its own (with **Ask AI** open, the list moves back above the form); on a phone it sits above the form. A change to the form itself (**How customers opt in**, **What you text and why**, a sample text, an answer to opting in, HELP or STOP, the **Privacy policy** or **Texting terms** link, or the **Business phone** or **Business email** when your website shows different ones) has **Approve change**: it puts the new text in that field and saves the form, and the change then shows **Approved**. Changes to your website pages are made on your website. Then click **Mark as ready** again.
3. The Granite Manager team reviews it and sends it to the carriers. There is no send button for the company. Before sending, the check runs again when it is more than a day old, since your pages may have changed; when it then finds changes, the registration goes back to **Draft** and you get them by email.

**Where it is** — the badge next to the title: **Draft**, **Ready to send**, **Sent to Telnyx** (the registry is checking the business), **In carrier review** (the carriers review how you text, usually a few days), **Approved** (numbers can text once assigned to the campaign), **Needs changes** (fix what is listed and mark it ready again) or **Suspended** (contact Granite Manager support).

Once the carriers have the campaign, only the sample texts, **How customers opt in** and the HELP answer can change: *The carriers have your campaign: only the sample texts, how customers agree and the HELP answer can change now.* Click **Save changes** after editing them.

**Messages under a field** (the form's own checks, before the AI check): *Enter the EIN as 9 digits, like 12-3456789.* · *Enter the 9-digit business number.* (Canada) · *The business must be registered in the US or Canada.* · *Enter the business website, starting with https://.* · *Enter the state or province as 2 letters.* · *Enter a valid ZIP or postal code.* · *Write at least 40 characters…* · *… must name the business.* · *… must say how to opt out, like "Reply STOP to opt out".* · *… uses a link shortener: carriers refuse them. Use the full link.* · *… repeats another: make each different.* · *A sample text has a link: say the texts carry links.* (tick **The texts contain links**) · *You say the texts carry links: a sample text must have one, or say they don't.* (the same for phone numbers) · *Write a sample text for each kind of texts you chose.* · *Keywords are single words of letters and digits…* · *The opt-out message must confirm they get no more texts…* · *The help message must say how to reach you…* · *Carriers require the opt-in message to say: …* (the words it is missing) · *Accept the carriers' terms for business texting.* (tick **Carrier rules**).
---

### What the Granite Manager team does (platform superusers)

**Where:** **Superuser Dashboard > Companies** → **Texting registrations (10DLC)** (every company's registration: *No registrations.* when none), or the company card's **⋯** → **10DLC texting**. The dialog *<company>: texting registration* shows the same form (editable, **Save changes**; *The company has not filled it out yet: this is the suggested first draft.* when the company never saved it) and a **Telnyx** part:

- The AI check's result: **Passed the AI check** (with its summary and *The AI could not verify these; check them by hand:* for what it could not tell), *The AI check could not run: review it by hand*, or the changes it asked for; *The AI is checking the form and the company's pages.* while it runs (the company's card shows this too).
- **Brand**, **Identity check** and **Campaign** statuses from Telnyx, with the **Brand id** and **Campaign id**, and **What the carriers said** when they refused.
- **Send to Telnyx** (only once the company marked it ready): *The campaign costs $<amount> up front* (read from Telnyx), then *Send to Telnyx? It charges for the brand and the campaign.* → **Yes, send** (*Sent to Telnyx.*). It needs the company's Telnyx setup saved first (*Save the company's Telnyx setup first (Companies → Telnyx): Telnyx reports to its webhook address.*).
- **Refresh** reads the statuses again from Telnyx.
- After a refusal, the team fixes the form (or the company does and marks it ready), optionally fills **What was fixed (appeal, optional)** (*for a fix outside the form, like a privacy policy added to the website*) and sends it again (*Sent to Telnyx again.*).
- **Numbers**: each of the company's active numbers with its campaign status (**Not assigned**, **ASSIGNED**, or a failure with the reason). **Assign numbers to the campaign** puts them on the approved campaign (*Numbers sent to Telnyx for the campaign.*). The numbers must be on the company's messaging profile (*The company's Telnyx setup has no messaging profile: numbers must be on one to be assigned.*); *The company has no active numbers yet.* when none.

---

### Common questions

- **Why can't we text yet?** The company needs a Telnyx messaging profile (set by a platform superuser) and an **Approved** texting registration.
- **I can't open the form.** Only users with the **Manager** position fill it out; a Manager with Admin access gives positions on **Admin > Users**.
- **It says Needs changes.** The carriers' reasons are listed on the card; fix those fields and click **Mark as ready** again.
- **Can the AI fill it in for me?** Click **Ask AI** in the form: it writes the text for any field from your form and company details, and you paste it in. Only you can type in the **Tax id (EIN)**, **Legal name** and address: they must match your IRS records (your CP 575 or 147C letter).

## Transactions — Employee & Admin (`/employee/transactions`, `/admin/transactions`)

**Transactions** lists every slab sale (transaction) in your company: who bought, who sold, which stones and bundles, sinks, square feet, and how far the job has gone (sold, cut, installed, cancelled). Office staff use it to follow jobs, open the sale contract, mark jobs installed, and (admins) rework or cancel a sale.

A transaction is created when a sales rep sells a slab from **Inventory > Stones** (**Sell** / **Sell Slab**). Customer, seller, prices, rooms and sinks of a sale are changed there (**Edit** on the sold slab, or **Unsell** to cancel) — not on the Transactions page. See **Employee Stones (Inventory & Selling Slabs)**.

**Three versions of the page:**

| Version | Sidebar | Who |
|---------|---------|-----|
| **Employee Transactions** | Employee view → **Transactions** (top-level item, not inside a section) | Every employee user |
| **Admin Transactions** | Admin view → **Transactions** (top-level item) | Admin users only |
| **Shop Transactions** | Shop portal → **Transactions** | Shop Worker / Shop Manager — see **Shop Worker — Transactions** |

All three show the page title **Sales Transactions**.

---

### Status of a transaction

The **Status** column is worked out automatically:

| Status | Color | Meaning |
|--------|-------|---------|
| **Sold** | Green | No slab on the sale is cut yet |
| **Partially Cut** | Gray | Some slabs cut, not all |
| **Cut** | Blue | Every slab is cut |
| **Installed** | Purple | Someone used **Mark as Installed** |
| **Cancelled** | Red | The sale was cancelled (Unsell, or **Delete** on Admin Transactions) |

Cut progress comes from the shop marking slabs **Cut** (shop portal, or the Cut buttons described below).

---

### Employee Transactions

#### Filters and search

| Control | Options | Default |
|---------|---------|---------|
| **Sales Rep** | **All**, or one seller (everyone who has sold something in your company) | **All** |
| **Status** | **In Progress** (not installed and not cancelled), **Finished** (installed or cancelled), **All Statuses** | **In Progress** |
| **Search transactions...** box + **Search** button | Text matched against customer name, seller, bundle and stone name | Empty |

- Typing 2 or more letters in the search box shows matching **customer names** below it; click one to filter by that name, or type any text and click **Search** (or press Enter).
- Filters and search are kept in the page address, so they stay when you open and close a transaction or refresh.

#### Table columns

All columns sort by clicking the header. 50 rows per page, newest sale first.

| Column | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| **Date** | Sale date |
| **Customer** | Customer name (blue) |
| **Sold By** | Seller |
| **Stone** | Stone name(s). Red and struck through = that slab was deleted from inventory |
| **Sqft** | The sale's square feet (**N/A** when not set) |
| **Sink** | Sink models on the sale; repeats show `x 2` etc. (**N/A** when none) |
