#### Marking a job installed

1. Find the sale (Status **Cut**). In its row click **⋯** → **Mark as Installed**.
   - The item is greyed out unless **every slab is cut** and the sale is not already installed or cancelled.
2. The **Mark Transaction as Installed** dialog opens:
   - **Installation Date** — defaults to today; change it if the install happened on another day.
   - **Paid** switch — on by default (**Mark as paid on same date**). Turn it off (**Do not mark as paid**) if the customer has not paid yet.
3. Click **Confirm** (or **Cancel**).
4. Toast: **Transaction marked as installed**. The status turns **Installed** (purple) and the sale moves from **In Progress** to **Finished**.

Possible errors: **Transaction is already marked as installed**, **Cannot mark as installed - not all slabs are cut**, **No slabs found for this transaction**.

There is no button to undo **Installed** or change the installation date afterwards. No email, SMS or notification is sent when a job is marked installed.

#### Opening the contract

**⋯** → **Contract** opens the sale's filled-in contract as a PDF in a new browser tab (print or download it from there).

#### Transaction Details (employee)

Click any row to open the **Transaction Details** dialog:

- **Sale Information** — **Customer**, **Sale Date**, **Sold By**, **Project Address** (**No address** when empty).
- **Sinks** — table of **Type** and **Price** with a **Total:** row, or *No sinks in this transaction*. Read-only.
- **Slabs** — **Bundle**, **Stone**, **SF**, **Status** (**Uncut** green / **Cut** blue), **Notes**, **Cut Date**, and a **Total Square Feet:** row.
  - **Cut** button on an uncut slab marks it cut with today's date.
  - **Uncut** button (red) on a cut slab reverses it.
  - The sale's status updates right away. Unlike the shop and Admin dialogs, these buttons do not remove or resize leftover (remnant) pieces.
- **Close** returns to the list with your filters.

Employees cannot record partial cuts, replace, remove or add slabs here — that is done in the shop portal or by an admin.

---

### Admin Transactions

Admin view → **Transactions**. Shows **all** sales of the company (every status, including installed and cancelled) for sellers whose user account still exists. There are no Sales Rep / Status filters.

#### Toolbar

- **Reports** button (blue) — opens the **Reports** page (cut-slab report). See **Statistics, Reports & Analytics**.
- **Search transactions...** — as you type, a dropdown lists up to 20 matching sales (customer, seller, bundle or stone), each with customer name, sale date, seller and project address. Click one to open it. Sales with no slabs are not listed.

#### Columns

**Date**, **Customer** (link that opens the sale), **Sold By**, **Stone**, **Sink**, **Sqft**, **Bundle**, **Status**, and an **Actions** menu (**⋯**) with **Edit** and **Delete**. Colors match the employee page. 50 rows per page, sortable headers.

Admin Transactions has no **Mark as Installed** or **Contract** — use Employee view → **Transactions** for those.

#### Editing a sale's slabs (Transaction Details, admin)

Click a row, the customer name, or **⋯** → **Edit**. The **Transaction Details** dialog shows:

- **Sale Information** — Customer, Sale Date, Sold By, Project Address.
- **Room Sinks** — sink models per room (e.g. `x2`), or **No sinks**. Read-only.
- **Rooms** — one table per room: **Bundle**, **Stone** (shows **(Partial)** for leftover pieces), **Status**, **Notes**, **Cut Date**, **Actions**, plus **Total sqft per room:** with a pencil to edit.
- Buttons: **Add Slab**, **Close**.

Slab **Actions** (⋯ menu):

| Action | What it does |
|--------|--------------|
| **Cut** / **Uncut** | Marks the slab cut (today) or reverses it. **Cut** also deletes that slab's unsold leftover pieces; **Uncut** resets leftover sizes to the full slab |
| **Partial** (uncut slabs) | **Mark as partially cut** — enter leftover **Length** and **Width**; **More left overs** saves and lets you add another piece, **Done** saves and marks the slab cut |
| **Replace** | **Replace Slab** dialog: pick another free bundle of the same stone (labeled **Full** or **Partial**); swaps immediately. On a cut slab you get **Uncut slab before replace** |
| **Remove** | **Remove Slab** confirm → **Delete**. Slab returns to inventory. The last slab cannot be removed (**Cannot remove last slab**) |

Other tools:

- **Add Slab** → **Select room** → search stones (**Search stones**, sold-out and hidden stones included) → pick a stone → click a free bundle. Toast **Slab added to sale**. The new slab copies the room's details (price, edge, square feet…) from the room's first slab.
- **New room name** + **Add Room** creates an empty room; it is saved only once a slab is added to it.
- **Total sqft per room** pencil → type a value (blank clears) → **Save** or Enter.

Success toasts: **Slab marked as cut**, **Slab marked as uncut**, **Slab replaced**, **Slab removed from sale**, **Slab added to sale**. Errors show **Could not update the sale**. Full step-by-step detail for these tools (they work the same in the shop portal) is in **Shop Worker — Transactions**.

#### Cancelling (deleting) a sale

1. In the row click **⋯** → **Delete**.
2. Dialog **Delete Transaction**: *Are you sure you want to delete the transaction for [customer]? This will cancel the sale and return all slabs and sinks to inventory.*
3. Click **Delete Transaction** (or **Cancel**).
4. Toast: **Transaction cancelled and items processed successfully**.

What happens: the sale is **cancelled**, not erased — it stays in the list with status **Cancelled** (red). Its slabs become available again, sinks and faucets on those slabs are freed, and unsold leftover pieces from partial slabs are removed (leftovers another sale already bought are kept). There is no undo; to sell the slabs again, create a new sale from **Inventory > Stones**. This is the same as **Unsell** in the sale form.

---

### Common questions / troubleshooting

- **How do I mark a slab as cut?** **Transactions** → open the sale (**Transaction Details**) → **Cut** on the slab's row (marks it cut with today's date; **Uncut** reverses it). Shop staff do it in the shop portal.
- **Mark as Installed is greyed out.** Not every slab is cut yet (status must be **Cut**), or the sale is already installed or cancelled. Have the shop mark the remaining slabs **Cut**, or use the **Cut** buttons in Transaction Details.
- **A sale disappeared from my list.** Employee **Status** defaults to **In Progress**, which hides installed and cancelled sales. Choose **All Statuses**, and set **Sales Rep** to **All**.
- **A sale is missing on Admin Transactions.** Sales whose seller's user account was deleted are not listed there; Employee Transactions still shows them.
- **How do I change the price, customer, seller or sink on a sale?** Not on Transactions. A sales rep opens the sold slab in **Inventory > Stones** and uses **Edit** (or **Unsell** to cancel).
- **How do I undo Installed?** There is no undo button in the app.
- **Where is the payroll / commission data?** Transactions only record the installation date and, with the **Paid** switch, a paid date. There is no payroll or pricing editor on Transactions. Commissions and payroll (based on signed quotes) are described in **Commissions**.
- **Why can't I partially cut or replace a slab from Employee Transactions?** Those tools are only in Admin Transactions and the shop portal.
- **Where are invoices?** QuickBooks invoices are on the customer's **Customer Information** (QuickBooks section). See **Invoices**.
- **A "sample" sale appeared.** It is a demo row for the guided tour; it is not saved.

## User positions & access

Each user has one or more **positions** (set on **Admin > Company settings > Users > Edit**). **Employee** portal access is automatic for everyone except users whose only positions are Marketing and/or Shop Worker. **Admin** portal access is a separate setting on the user. Some positions lock a user into one single-purpose portal regardless of that.

| Position | Portal / Access | Key pages |
|----------|----------------|-----------|
| **Sales Rep** | Employee CRM. Cannot be combined with Shop Worker. | Dashboard, Inventory, CRM (Customers, Deals, Emails, SMS), Quotes, Schedule, Transactions, Resources, Operations, My Account, Samples |
| **Sales Manager** | Same as Sales Rep, plus **Invalid** and **Delete** in the Customers row menu (admins without this position don't get them), Telegram lead alerts and assigning incoming leads | Same as Sales Rep |
| **Shop Manager** | Adds **Maintenance** (shop equipment) to the Employee/Admin sidebar and is the only position that can edit equipment and checks there; also opens the shop **Transactions** page. Other access as for any employee. | Maintenance, Shop Transactions |
| **Shop Worker** | Shop app only. Cannot be combined with Sales Rep. | Shop: Transactions, Samples, Maintenance, My Account |
| **Manager** | Unlocks **Company settings > Billing** (Employee and Admin sidebars; Admin access not needed). With Admin access it also unlocks **Company settings > Users** and **Company settings > Company** (sales tax, logo, address). | Company settings > Users / Company / Billing |
| **Installer** | Installer portal only | Tabs **Schedule**, **Map**, **Checklist** (fill and sign post-install checklists, works offline). No Invoices tab: an installer sees only the invoice the office linked to the job, in **Event details** |
| **Template Guy** | Template schedule portal only: the technician's own templating appointments. Also chooses who sees an Instruction (**Visible to**). | Template schedule (**My Schedule**) |
| **Marketing** | External Marketing portal only | Leads, Add lead, Edit lead, Delete lead, walk-in stats, deal-by-stage summary |
| **Walk-in** | Walk-in check-in form only | Walk-in check-in |
| **Super Admin** | Admin and Employee access in each assigned company; switch companies from the header. **Users**, **Company** and **Billing** still need the Manager position, which only applies in the home company. Only a platform superuser can edit or delete a Super Admin. | Employee + Admin pages for each assigned company |
| **Office Manager** | Employee CRM label. With a CloudTalk or RingCentral line set up, customer texts (estimate booking confirmations and reminders, post-install survey links) are sent from that person's number. | — |
| **Inventory Manager** | Opens only its sections: by default Inventory (Employee and Admin stones, sinks, faucets), Customers (with their deals, quotes and drawings), Transactions, Samples and Special Order, plus My Account. Each company changes these in **Position access** on the Company page. | Inventory, Customers, Transactions, Samples, Special Order |
| **Scheduling Manager** | Opens only its sections: by default Customers and Schedule, plus My Account. Changed in **Position access**. | Customers, Schedule |

**Inventory Manager / Scheduling Manager:** the section limits apply only to someone whose positions are just these (holding **Sales Rep**, **Sales Manager**, **Manager** or **Super Admin** beside them gives the whole app; platform superusers are never limited). They land on their first section's page; the sidebar shows only their sections, other pages don't open, and My Account, Report a Bug, the AI chat and Billing always stay. **Admin > Company settings > Company** → **Position access** (*What someone with only these positions can open*): tick or untick each section per position (**Dashboard**, **Inventory**, **Inventory (admin)**, **Customers**, **Deals**, **Quotes**, **Emails**, **SMS**, **Schedule**, **Schedule (admin)**, **Transactions**, **Samples**, **Special Order**, **Checklists**, **Suppliers, Supports, Documents, Images, Instructions**); it saves at once. **Reset to default** puts a changed position back.

**Position + access combinations:**
- **Admin > Company settings > Users / Company** need Admin access plus the **Manager** position (platform superusers always see them). **Billing** needs only the Manager position in the current company.
- If a user holds more than one portal position, the first of **Installer**, **Walk-in**, **Marketing**, **Shop Worker**, **Template Guy** decides the only portal they can open. Super Admins and platform superusers are never locked (a Super Admin who is also a Template Guy keeps the full CRM and gets **My Schedule** in the Employee sidebar).
- Locked users can still sign out and reset their password; every other page sends them back to their portal.
- When the company's Granite Manager subscription needs payment, users are sent to the **Billing** page until it is resolved.
- Platform superusers (Granite Manager staff) can preview the screens as **Installer**, **Template**, **Marketing** or **Check-in** with the position selector in the header.

---

## Walk-in check-in (`/customer/:companyId/check-in`)

The walk-in check-in page is the sign-in form for visitors to your showroom. It usually runs on a tablet or computer at the front desk. Each visitor reads the safety instructions, enters their contact details and taps **Submit**. That creates a **Walk-in** customer in the CRM, and the form clears for the next visitor.

**Address:** `/customer/<company ID>/check-in`. There is no sidebar item for it. It is the home page of the Walk-in account.

---

### Who can open it

- The page needs a signed-in account of your company. If nobody is signed in, it goes to the sign-in page.
- Users with the **Walk-in** position land on this page when they sign in. They cannot open any other page (only this form, logout and password reset).
- Any other signed-in staff user can also open the address directly.
- If the address has another company's number, the page switches to your own company's form.

#### Setting up a kiosk account

1. Ask a platform superuser to create the kiosk user with the **Walk-in** position. The Walk-in position is hidden from everyone else in **Admin > Company settings > Users**.
2. Sign in on the kiosk device with that account. The check-in form opens automatically and stays signed in on that device (up to 60 days).

---

### Page layout

- **Header:** company logo, company name and **Logout**. No sidebar.
- Heading **Safety Instructions**, then **We kindly ask you to:** with six rules:
  1. Refrain from moving slabs or remnants by yourself.
  2. Avoid leaning on countertops and be cautious of sharp edges.
  3. Keep children supervised.
  4. Stay within designated areas.
  5. Use caution on slippery surfaces.
  6. Report any concerns.

The safety text is fixed and cannot be edited.

---

### Form fields

| Field | Required | Notes |
|-------|----------|-------|
| **Name** | Yes | Placeholder **Your full name**. Words are capitalized automatically. |
| **Phone** | Yes | Format `123-456-7890`; must be a valid US number |
| **Email** | No | Must be a valid email if filled |
| **Project Address** | No | Start typing (at least 3 characters) and pick an address from the suggestions |
| **How did you hear about us?** | No | Google, Facebook, Referral, Flyer, Drive-thru, Instagram, Other |
| Acknowledgment checkbox | Yes | **I acknowledge that I have read, understand, and agree to the safety instructions** |

If the company has CloudTalk or RingCentral connected, the checkbox text continues **and agree with Terms and Conditions**. The **Terms and Conditions** link opens **Terms and Conditions & Privacy Policy**. It says calls and SMS may be recorded, and that the visitor agrees to receive transactional and promotional SMS from the company (reply HELP for help or STOP to opt out). Close it with **Close**.

---

### Checking in a visitor

1. The visitor fills in the form and ticks the acknowledgment box.
2. They tap **Submit**.
3. On success, a toast shows **Walk-in successful**, **Thank you. We look forward to assisting you!**, and the form clears.

#### Duplicate check

Before saving, the page checks whether the phone or email already belongs to one of your customers. If it does, a red **Possible duplicate found** dialog opens:

- **Customer** — the existing customer's name.
- **Sales rep** — their sales rep, or **Unassigned**.
- **If this is the same person, please avoid creating a duplicate to keep records clean.**
- **Clear form** — empties the form. The visitor is **not** saved.

Returning customers are not saved a second time. Staff can find them in **CRM > Customers** with **Find Customer**.

#### Error messages

- **Name is required**
- **Phone number must be exactly 12 characters (e.g., 123-456-7890)**, **Format must be XXX-XXX-XXXX.**, **Invalid US phone number or area code.**
- **Invalid email address**
- **You must acknowledge the safety instructions**

---

### What happens in the CRM

- A new customer is created with source **Walk-in**. The name, phone, email, project address and **How did you hear about us?** answer are saved.
- No sales rep is assigned, and no deal is created yet.
- Staff see the visitor in **CRM > Customers** on the **Walk-in** tab (the default tab). Rows with no sales rep are red.
- Assign a sales rep from the **Sales Rep** column or by editing the customer. Assigning a rep can create the deal on the default pipeline stage.
- Walk-ins are counted in Admin statistics (walk-in breakdowns) and on the Marketing portal's **Walk-ins** tab.

---

### Common questions

- **Why does the check-in page go to the login page?** Nobody is signed in on that device. Sign in with the kiosk (Walk-in) account or a staff account.
- **I can't find the Walk-in position when editing a user.** Only a platform superuser can assign it.
- **Why didn't the visitor get a sales rep or a deal?** Walk-ins are never assigned automatically. Assign a rep in **CRM > Customers**.
- **The visitor saw "Possible duplicate found".** They are already in your customer list. Look them up with **Find Customer** instead of creating a new record.
- **How do I leave the kiosk page?** Click **Logout** in the header.
